🎯 The Role
We are hiring a Product Operations Manager to make Medify's product organisation more effective as we scale.
You will own and continuously improve the systems, processes, tooling and insights that help Product, Engineering, Design and Learning work together consistently and deliver better products, faster. You will enable Product Managers to spend more time on strategy, customer discovery, prioritisation and outcomes by removing operational friction and creating trusted ways of working.
This is not a Product Manager or delivery manager role. The Head of Product and Product Managers remain accountable for product strategy, priorities and deciding what we build and why. You will improve the system in which those decisions are turned into high-quality delivery.
🧠 What You'll Do
Own the product operating system
Maintain and continuously improve Medify's product playbook, templates and documentation.
Standardise discovery outputs, product requirements, ticket writing, refinement and handover practices across squads.
Improve the cadence for roadmaps, OKRs, planning, reporting, showcases and retrospectives.
Make ownership, decision points and handoffs clear across Product, Engineering, Design and Learning.
Introduce lightweight processes where they add value, and remove processes or meetings that no longer do.
Improve the Product–Engineering operational interface
Partner closely with the Engineering Managers on refinement, backlog standards, planning logistics, workflows, delivery reporting and release processes.
Identify recurring bottlenecks and help teams resolve their root causes.
Follow up actions from retrospectives and cross-functional reviews so improvements are completed.
Support consistent documentation, product QA, release checklists and feature flag governance.
Escalate strategic trade-offs, capacity decisions and major organisational risks to the Head of Product and Engineering Managers.
Own product tooling and AI workflows
Own and improve the product team's internal tooling, including Notion, GitHub, product templates and analytics tools such as PostHog.
Identify repetitive work that can be simplified or automated.
Design and maintain practical AI workflows that improve PM productivity and quality.
Establish clear conventions and governance so tools remain trusted and easy to use.
Evaluate new tools based on measurable team needs rather than novelty.
Strengthen product insight and reporting
Maintain trusted product dashboards and product health reporting.
Coordinate customer feedback and help create a usable, searchable insight repository.
Bring together evidence from analytics, interviews, support and product usage.
Track feature adoption and surface trends, risks and opportunities.
Produce concise, decision-useful reporting for Product leadership and the wider business.
Enable and develop the product team
Build onboarding and training resources for new Product Managers and Associate Product Managers.
Coach colleagues on Medify's product processes, tools and documentation standards.
Share effective practices across squads while allowing teams appropriate autonomy.
Organise product showcases and improve how learning travels through the organisation.
Help Product Managers spend more of their time with customers and solving the right problems.
🤝 How You'll Work with Product and Engineering Leadership
You will be the primary owner of the day-to-day operational interface between Product and Engineering.
The Head of Product and Engineering Managers will continue to jointly own strategic priorities, capacity trade-offs, squad structure, major delivery risks, hiring and organisational decisions. You will make those conversations more effective by ensuring the underlying processes, information and follow-through are reliable.
A useful distinction is:
Product leadership decides what we build and why.
Product Operations improves how we work together to deliver it.
✅ What Success Looks Like
Within your first 12 months:
Product Managers spend more time on customer discovery, strategy and outcomes.
Ideas move from discovery into delivery with less avoidable delay.
Refinement is more effective and tickets consistently meet agreed standards.
Product documentation is current, easy to find and trusted.
Roadmap status, product health and delivery risks are visible and reliable.
Product and Engineering leaders spend less time resolving recurring operational friction.
New Product Managers and Associate Product Managers become productive more quickly.
Teams use practical AI and automation workflows that save time or improve quality.
Actions from retrospectives and process reviews lead to measurable improvements.
Product, Engineering, Design and Learning report clearer and more consistent ways of working.
🧭 About You
Essential
Experience in Product Operations, Product Management, Programme Management or a closely related role in a technology organisation.
A track record of building or improving product processes in a scaling company.
Excellent written communication and documentation skills.
Strong organisational skills and the ability to turn ambiguity into simple, workable systems.
Experience with product and delivery tooling such as Notion, Jira and analytics platforms.
Data literacy and confidence using qualitative and quantitative evidence.
Comfortable influencing across functions without relying on formal authority.
A continuous-improvement mindset, with good judgement about when process helps and when it gets in the way.
Comfortable working independently in a high-autonomy, remote environment.
Nice to have
Experience in EdTech, SaaS or another digital product business.
Experience using product analytics tools such as PostHog.
SQL or hands-on analytics experience.
Experience implementing OKRs, roadmaps or product operating cadences.
Experience designing internal AI workflows or automations.
Experience supporting product quality, experimentation or release governance.
🏢 How We Work
Fully remote and highly flexible. We care about impact, not hours.
High trust and autonomy, with no micromanagement.
Product decisions are evidence-led and made close to the people with the relevant context.
We favour clear ownership and lightweight processes.
Personal development goals are prioritised over rigid performance metrics.
✅ What We Offer
Competitive salary depending on criteria fulfilment.
Salary progression linked to impact and responsibility.
Annual salary increment and bonus depending on company performance.
Pension contributions.
Private healthcare and dental cover.
Annual learning and development budget.
Full flexibility over where, when and how you work.
Annual company retreat.
Work alongside highly competent Product, Engineering, Design and Learning teams.
High independence and meaningful ownership from day one.
🚀 Why Join
This role has leverage across every Medify product and squad. The systems you improve will help teams make better decisions, collaborate more effectively and deliver higher-quality experiences for learners.
You will have the freedom to shape how a growing product organisation operates, remove friction that affects multiple teams, and create practical improvements that compound over time.

## Senior Electrochemical Stack Engineer
****About Mission Zero Technologies****
****We’re a London-based climate tech startup working to reinvent carbon for a thriving planet. Since 2020, we have rapidly pioneered the world’s most versatile direct air capture (DAC) technology to recover historic CO2 emissions from the atmosphere, anywhere at any scale. Backed by Breakthrough Energy Ventures, the XPRIZE foundation, Stripe, and the UK Government, we’ve moved a brand new climate technology from lab to commercial plants in under three years to rapidly empower carbon removal and sustainable utilisation.****
## About the role
Join MZT at a pivotal moment as we transition from an early-stage R&D startup to a revenue-generating company ready to scale our direct-air capture technology globally.
We're looking for an Electrochemical Stack Engineer to develop our next generation of stack designs. Electrodialytic approaches to DAC lean on established electrodialysis designs, however these designs are far from optimal for the specificity of electrochemical direct-air capture. As our Electrochemical Stack Engineer you'll lead stack development at MZT. You'll define the opportunity areas for our next-generation stack, develop concepts that attack the biggest resistance losses in the cell, while ensuring stability and robustness, and lead the build–test–evaluate cycles that prove (or kill) them. For winning concepts, you'll scale them into full-size stacks, navigating supply chain and manufacturing constraints along the way.
The role has two sides. You'll lead on the stacks we procure, assessing what the supply chain offers, judging their suitability for our process and specifying modifications where needed. In parallel, you'll lead the development of DAC-optimised electrodialytic stacks designed around our process conditions from the start. On both fronts you'll work closely with our process, mechanical and electrical engineers so that the stack meets the requirements of our DAC technology and the wider plant design.
Reporting to the R&D leadership team, you'll work alongside key members of the R&D lab, and mentor junior scientists and engineers as the team grows.
## What you’ll be doing
* Defining the opportunity areas for MZT's next-generation electrochemical stack: quantifying where the losses sit and which are worth attacking first
* Developing concepts for performance improvement across cell geometry, materials and flow design, backed by models and analysis that clarify your predictions
* Leading build–test–evaluate cycles with the R&D team: designing testing campaigns, characterising stack performance and tracing observed phenomena back to underlying mechanisms and design features
* Scaling successful concepts into full-scale stacks, working through fabrication, assembly and design-for-manufacture constraints
* Leading stack procurement: assessing commercially available stacks, specifying modifications and managing technical relationships with vendors and manufacturers
* Articulating stack requirements to process, mechanical, electrical and safety engineers so the stack and the wider plant design converge
* Closing the feedback loop: internalising learnings from every campaign and applying them to subsequent stack designs
* Mentoring, guiding and supporting junior staff, helping them acquire new skills, knowledge and capabilities
## What you’ll need to be successful in this role
* A deep grounding in the theory and mathematical principles that describe electrochemical processes. You understand electrochemistry from first principles, not just by analogy or heuristics
* Experience designing electrochemical stacks at multiple scales involving aqueous electrolytes, ion-exchange membranes and gas generation
* A strong grasp of how the culmination of geometric features, material selection and process parameters determines the critical performance parameters of a stack
* A track record of taking designs through to fabricated, assembled hardware in collaboration with mechanical, electrical and process engineers
* Significant experience designing and executing testing campaigns, with the diagnostic instinct to trace behaviour back to root mechanisms
* The habit of reducing problems to first principles and building models to sharpen your thinking, paired with the judgement to reach for heuristics when they're the better tool
* Equal appetite for ideation and execution: you can get obsessed with a problem, and you finish what you start
* As comfortable in the lab or workshop as you are developing designs, models and analysis
* Experience mentoring, guiding or supervising junior colleagues
* A degree in chemical engineering, electrochemical engineering, materials science or a related discipline
* Roughly 5–10 years' experience spanning stack design, testing and scale-up
* Clear communication skills across engineering disciplines
## Ideally, you’ll also have:
* Direct experience with electrodialysis, bipolar membranes or related ion-exchange membrane processes
* Hands-on experience with carbonate or alkaline electrolytes, and with managing gas evolution and two-phase flow inside cells
* Electrochemical or multiphysics modelling experience (COMSOL or equivalent, or your own codes)
* Experience with EIS and other advanced electrochemical diagnostics
* Working CAD skills, enough to take your own concepts from sketch to drawing
* Experience working directly with stack, membrane or component manufacturers, and navigating their manufacturing constraints
* A PhD in electrochemistry, electrochemical engineering or a related field
* Experience in a startup or similarly fast-moving R&D environment
* Patents or publications in electrochemical cell or stack design

## Our Process
**We've outlined below what our typical process looks like, this can vary slightly depending upon the role or team you've applied for. Our goal is to provide a positive and accessible experience for all applicants, ensuring everyone has the support they need to showcase their best selves.**
Our resourcing team are on hand to help with any questions about your application and you can reach them by e-mailing resourcing@morrisonsplc.co.uk.
* 1
### Find an opportunity that's right for you
Once you've found a role that's right for you, you can apply via this site. If it's your first time applying with us then we'll need all your essential information and we might ask you to upload your most recent CV. If you've applied for roles with us before then we should recognise you and you won't need to share these details again, unless something has changed that you need to update us on.
* 2
### Online Assessment (Customer Assistant roles)
After your application, we might send you an e-mail and ask you to complete an online assessment. This is typically a situation judgement test where we'll ask you ten questions with mutliple choice answers and takes around 10-15 minutes to complete. The questions will give you a feel for the types of scenarios you might encounter working in our stores - think customer first.
* 3
### Let's find out more
For some of our stores and site roles, if you've been successful with your application we might just e-mail and ask you to book a slot for your interview. For other roles our resourcing team will get in touch with you to find out a bit more about you and why you applied. They'll also answer any questions you might have about us and the role. After all, it's a two way process!
* 4
### Interview
Our interviews are typically face to face but can sometimes be virtual. Don't worry, we'll advise either way. Your interview can differ depending on the role or team. Part of the interview may include some competency questions against our Ways of Working (listed below).
* 5
### Final Stage
With some of our roles there might be a second interveiw. This tends to be for roles in our Head Office and some salaried positions across our stores and sites. As part of this second stage, we might ask you to complete a task, such as a SWOT analysis or something similar, and present it back during the interview. This helps us understand your approach and thinking about the role.
* 6
### Decision
Our resourcing team or the store or site you've applied to will be in touch with you as soon as they can to let you know the outcome. If you've been successful we'll share the details of our offer with you and follow up with everything you need on e-mail.

At Formula 1, we are passionate about delivering the world’s greatest sports and entertainment spectacle leaving a positive legacy wherever we race. Now, more than 75 years on, the sport remains a pioneer, developing technologies that have made a significant impact on society beyond the track.

Our team of skilled technical experts keeps Formula 1 moving, and as a Distribution Engineer, you will play a vital role in ensuring the reliable delivery of all video and audio feeds that power F1’s global broadcast and digital output.
Based at the Formula 1 Media & Technology Centre in Biggin Hill, you will provide crucial operational support during race weekends - establishing, monitoring, and routing feeds essential to live production and worldwide distribution.
Outside of event weekends, you will contribute to ongoing upgrades across our technology stack, improving reliability, performance, and scalability to meet the growing distribution demands of the sport.

* Manage the switching of services during normal and emergency conditions to ensure all outputs remain on air.
* Liaise with thirdparty fibre, uplink and connectivity providers during fault investigations.
* Routinely check the health and performance of all contribution and distribution equipment.
* Proactively identify and mitigate risks or vulnerabilities across the distribution infrastructure.
* Develop a solid understanding of Formula 1’s broader technical ecosystem and how operational departments collaborate during race weekends.
* Create and maintain documentation, diagrams and operational procedures.
* Implement, or support the implementation of, upgrades, changes and improvements to distribution systems and infrastructure.

A technically strong, calm under pressure engineer who thrives in a live broadcast environment and is committed to delivering highly reliable services during the most demanding operational windows of the F1 season.
**Experience**
*Prior to the role it would be essential that you:*
* Have experience working in a broadcast, media, or telecommunications environment.
* Ideally have experience within Live Sports or similarly high-pressure operational contexts.
*Some desirable experience that you may bring to the role:*
* Experience working directly with high availability distribution or transmission systems.
* Familiarity with troubleshooting real time broadcast chain issues across multiple vendors, technologies and signal types.
* Previous experience supporting projects involving system upgrades or infrastructure modernisation.
**Knowledge & Skills**
*Prior to the role it is essential that you demonstrate:*
* In-depth knowledge of television distribution systems, platforms and standards.
* Working knowledge of HD & 3GSDI baseband video signals.
* Understanding of AES, MADI, Dolby E and AES67 audio signals.
* Good practical knowledge of TCP/IP networking, including multicast traffic.
* Experience with SMPTE 2110 standards.
* Working knowledge of h.264/h.265/HEVC encoding configuration.
* Understanding of MPEG2 Transport Streams and TR101290 analysis.
* Hands-on experience with control/monitoring systems such as Cerebrum, TAG or Data-miner.
* Ability to operate signal test and analysis equipment for both baseband and
* transport stream workflows.
* Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain technical issues to both technical and nontechnical stakeholders.
* Ability to remain focused and effective in high-pressure, time-critical environments.
**Qualifications**
*Not essential to be successful in the role but you may also have the following qualifications:*
* Certifications related to broadcast engineering, IT networking, or media transport (e.g., SMPTE, Cisco, or equivalent).
* Vendor-specific training linked to encoding, routing, monitoring, or IP-based media workflows.
**Personal Qualities**
*In this role it is essential that you are:*
* Calm and composed when working under pressure.
* Methodical, detail oriented and proactive in identifying potential issues before they impact service.
* Adaptable, with the ability to switch focus quickly during live operational environments.
* A clear communicator who builds trust with colleagues and external partners.
* Willing to work unsociable hours, including weekends, when supporting live race events.

* Private Healthcare scheme
* Dental Care

* Enhanced maternity/paternity leave and other family planning policies
* A free staff shuttle service running to and from surrounding trains stations near to Biggin Hill
* Free healthy snacks in our offices
* Subsidised canteen in Biggin Hill, serving breakfast and lunch
* 25 days annual leave and 8 Bank Holiday days, plus a Christmas period closure
* Opportunities to develop and request training for your role via our in-house Learning and Development team
* Discount on F1 merchandise

London

OverviewApplication
Multiverse is the upskilling platform for AI and Tech adoption.
We have partnered with 1,500+ companies to deliver a new kind of learning that's transforming today’s workforce.
Our upskilling apprenticeships are designed for people of any age and career stage to build critical AI, data, and tech skills. Our learners have driven $2bn+ ROI for their employers, using the skills they’ve learned to improve productivity and measurable performance.
In April 2026, we announced $70 million in strategic funding, led by Schroders Capital, with participation from StepStone Group, Lightspeed Venture Partners and General Catalyst. At an increased valuation of $2.1bn, the round makes us Europe’s first EdTech double unicorn.
But we aren’t stopping there. With a strong operational footprint and 800+ employees, we have ambitious plans to continue scaling. We’re building a world where tech skills unlock people’s potential and output. Join Multiverse and power our mission to equip the workforce to win in the AI era.
## **The opportunity**
Enterprise Trust & Reliability (ETR) turns enterprise trust into enterprise revenue. It's where enterprise buyers decide whether they can adopt us: the compliance posture and evidence base we sell on, the operational reliability that keeps us dependable at scale, and the integrations and partnerships that make Multiverse procurement-ready. Far from a support function, it's the layer that makes enterprise adoption possible and drives client partnerships and revenue at scale.
You'll lead the engineering for two of ETR's groups, Commercial Tech & Integrations and Stability & Operations: around seven engineers across the two, and the mandate to shape how they work.
## **Why the role exists**
ETR is a newly formed function, built by bringing commercial integrations and operational reliability together because enterprise buyers make or break AI deals on exactly those things. You're the first dedicated engineering manager for these teams, with the mandate to build how they work from here: technical direction alongside the tech leads, delivery rhythm, growth plans, the hiring bar, on-call practice, all of it. You’ll report into the Single Threaded Leader for the function and together you will shape an evolving function - if you want to set the technical playbook, this is the role.
## **The teams you'll lead**
**Commercial Tech & Integrations (CTI)** bridges what we sell and what we ship, making Multiverse demonstrable, sellable, and procurement-ready. It owns key cross functional services, CRM data flows into product, customer onboarding friction reduction, and integrations into customer systems (e.g. LMS/KMS). It also runs vendor and partner integrations, including Anthropic. The engineering challenge is building clean, well-tested APIs and integrations that hold up under enterprise security reviews.
**Stability & Operations (S&O)** keeps the platform dependable as it scales: incident management and the severity model, service-level objectives (SLOs) and error budgets, observability and DORA (DevOps Research and Assessment) delivery metrics, the on-call rotation, and the technology evidence base the business needs as it approaches IPO. The engineering challenge here is reliability designed in rather than bolted on, and a fast, calm path from "something's wrong" to "it's fixed."
Between them, these two teams carry the things enterprise buyers test hardest: can you integrate with us cleanly, and will you stay up. You own the engineering health and delivery of both.
## **What you'll do**
You'll own delivery, technical direction, and team health across CTI and S&O:
* **Lead the engineers.** Line-manage the seven-or-so engineers across the two groups: growth plans, coaching, performance, and wellbeing, to a high bar, with no surprises at review time.
* **Own delivery and technical direction.** Partner with the tech leads on architecture, and hold the standard for how the teams design, review, and ship across two quite different technical domains.
* **Hire and raise the bar.** Fill the open seats using our High-Agency & AI-Native question bank and a live AI build stage, and build a team that stays strong as it grows.
* **Drive an AI-native operating rhythm.** Engineers using Claude Code and agentic tooling hard, with tighter discovery-to-build-to-review loops, and you modelling it in how you run the teams.
* **Own the operational backbone.** On-call health, incident practice, and clear, proactive communication when things go wrong, so reliability is a habit rather than a fire drill.
## **What we're looking for**
* **Engineering management at depth.** You've managed engineers building and running production systems, and you can speak to the teams you've grown, the delivery you've owned, and the performance calls you've made.
* **Technical range across both domains.** You needn't be the deepest expert in either, but you hold your own with senior engineers on both sides: integration and API design, identity and SSO, and third-party systems on the CTI side; reliability, observability, incident response, and SLOs on the S&O side. You can steer a design review, challenge an estimate, and make a sensible build-versus-buy or sequencing call. This isn't a hands-on coding seat, but it is an engineering one.
* **Delivery through ambiguity.** You've kept teams shipping when the structure wasn't fixed, and can talk to how you balanced pace, quality, and people.
* **You grow people.** Engineers you've coached, mentored, or levelled up, and a real preference for people leadership as the job.
* **AI-native by default.** You work with AI tooling day to day and expect your engineers to, and you can tell AI-assisted speed from AI-shaped slop.
## **What we offer**
Pre-IPO equity with runway to vest before a potential exit. An AI-native engineering environment built around tools like Claude Code. And dynamic re-teaming: you accumulate breadth across missions rather than depth in one fixed lane, and your development travels with you through every team change. Because this mandate is first-of-its-kind, you're defining how engineering management works here, not stepping into someone else's template.
## ## **Not for you if**
You want to stay predominantly hands-on in the code (we value and pay the engineering track equally), or you see management as a stepping stone rather than the work itself.
**Benefits**
* **Time off** - 27 days holiday, plus 5 additional days off: 1 life event day, 2 volunteer days, 2 company-wide wellbeing days (M-Powered Weekend) and 8 bank holidays per year
* **Health & Wellness**- private medical Insurance with Bupa, a medical cashback scheme, life insurance, gym membership & wellness resources through Wellhub and access to Spill - all in one mental health support
* **Hybrid work offering** - for most roles we collaborate in the office three days per week with the exception of Coaches and Instructors who collaborate in the office once a month
* **Work-from-anywhere scheme** - you'll have the opportunity to work from anywhere, up to 10 days per year
* **Space to connect:** Beyond the desk, we make time for weekly catch-ups, seasonal celebrations, and have a kitchen that’s always stocked!
**Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion**
We’re an equal opportunities employer. And proud of it. Every applicant and employee is afforded the same opportunities regardless of race, colour, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression, or veteran status. This will never change. Read our Equality, Diversity & Inclusion policy here.
**Our Commitment to Safeguarding**
Multiverse is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of our learners. We expect all employees to share this commitment and adhere to our Safeguarding Policy, our Prevent Policy and all other Multiverse company policies. Successful applicants will be required to undertake at least a Basic check via the Disclosure Barring Service (DBS).
For roles that will involve a Regulated Activity, successful applicants must also undergo an Enhanced DBS check, including a Children’s Barred List check and a Prohibition Order check. Roles involving Regulated Activity may interact with vulnerable groups, therefore are exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 meaning applicants are required to declare any convictions, cautions, reprimands, and final warnings.

## Job Description
**About the job.**
National Highways has an excellent opportunity for an Assistant Project Manager to join the Integration & Enablement (I&E) team within Major Projects on the A66 programme. The I&E team works across the programme to improve alignment, coordination and future readiness in areas including communications and stakeholder engagement, lands, utilities, traffic management, operational collaboration and futureproofing.
As an Assistant Project Manager, you will support Project Managers and workstream leads in turning agreed strategies and priorities into clear, practical plans. You will coordinate information across work packages and specialist functions, maintain visibility of milestones, dependencies, risks and decisions, and support governance, performance reporting, handover and continuous improvement.
Please note this position can be based from either our Manchester or Leeds offices; however, travel to the A66, will be required.
* Support the development, implementation and review of I&E strategies, workstream plans and delivery arrangements, ensuring agreed actions are practical, clearly owned and aligned with programme priorities.
* Develop and maintain proportionate project and programme management products, including integrated plans, milestone and look-ahead schedules, action trackers, risk and issue records, decision logs, governance products and handover packs.
* Coordinate inputs from work package teams, specialist functions, stakeholders, delivery partners and the supply chain to identify key milestones, interfaces, dependencies, constraints, commitments and decisions required to support effective delivery.
* Support the preparation of reports and briefing information, maintaining actions and commitments, tracking project readiness and progress, and highlighting matters requiring intervention or escalation.
* Analyse project and workstream information to identify emerging risks, gaps, inconsistencies and potential impacts on future activities, and support the development and monitoring of mitigation or recovery actions.
* Support the Project Manager in day-to-day project activities, including commercial and contract administration, health and safety, risk, quality and assurance.
**About you.**
* Suitable project management qualification or equivalent relevant experience, ideally with membership of, or a commitment to work towards membership of, an appropriate professional body (i.e. APM).
* Experience of supporting project or programme delivery in a complex, multi-disciplinary or matrix environment.
* Good understanding of health and safety, quality and governance requirements within project delivery.
* Strong organisational and planning skills, with the ability to coordinate several activities, maintain accurate records and manage competing priorities.
* Strong collaboration, stakeholder, communication and presentation skills, with the confidence to bring together contributions from a wide range of teams and disciplines.
* Good analytical and constructive challenge skills, with the ability to interpret project information, identify gaps or inconsistencies, provide clear commentary and escalate concerns through agreed governance routes is desirable.
**About us.**
Here at National Highways, we manage and improve England's motorways and major A roads, helping our customers have safer, smoother and more reliable journeys. Our priorities are safety, customers and delivery, and at the core of this are our values of passion, integrity, safety, teamwork and ownership.
Major Projects is responsible for major enhancements to our road network. We make roads safer, journeys more reliable and unlock economic growth. At the same time, we seek out ways to create opportunities for sustainable travel, help nature to thrive and support our journey to net zero carbon.
Our teams work closely with the supply chain to design and construct road projects, as well as develop a pipeline of possible projects as we look to the future. Our skills span many areas, from customer experts and land and property advisers to project management. We understand the potential that our road schemes can bring.

## Summary
\*\*\*INTERNAL AND PARTNER APPLICANTS ONLY PLEASE\*\*\* Applications will only be considered from current employees of the National Trust, National Lottery Heritage Fund, and Natural England.
We're looking for an Advocacy Manager to lead the development and delivery of advocacy activity across the Nature Towns and Cities coalition.
**About the role profile**: This role is being recruited using the National Trust's External Affairs Consultant (Grade 5) role profile and will be known internally by this title. While the profile reflects the broad skills, knowledge and experience required, the responsibilities and focus of this post are most accurately described in this advert.
**If you would like to discuss this role please contact info@naturetownsandcities.org.uk**
## What it's like to work here
This is a high-profile role that will build understanding, awareness and support for the Nature Towns and Cities mission among political decision-makers and key stakeholders across the UK. Working across a unique coalition of partners, you'll help ensure the benefits of urban nature are understood by politicians, policy-makers and sector leaders, while strengthening relationships that support delivery of the programme.
Nature Towns and Cities is working to put nature and green space at the heart of towns, cities and neighbourhoods across the UK. Through this role, you'll help build the partnerships, visibility and political support needed to enable long-term action and investment in urban nature.
## What you'll be doing
You'll lead the delivery of the Nature Towns and Cities advocacy strategy, building awareness, understanding and support for the programme among political audiences and stakeholders across Westminster, Holyrood, Cardiff Bay and Stormont. This includes helping decision-makers understand the scale of unequal access to nature and the role Nature Towns and Cities can play in addressing it.
A confident relationship-builder, you'll develop and maintain networks with parliamentarians, government officials, local government leaders, metro mayors, city and regional partners, sector organisations and other influential stakeholders across all four nations who can champion the programme and its goals.
Working across the coalition will be your natural mode. You'll collaborate with colleagues from Natural England, the National Lottery Heritage Fund, the National Trust and a growing range of partners across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland to identify opportunities and tailor engagement approaches to different political and policy contexts while maintaining a coherent UK-wide narrative.
You'll help tell the story of Nature Towns and Cities by developing briefings, presentations and stakeholder engagement materials that demonstrate the impact of the programme and showcase action taking place in towns and cities across the UK.
You'll monitor political and policy developments across all four nations, identifying opportunities for engagement and providing insight to programme partners. While the role does not undertake party-political activity or lobbying on behalf of individual organisations, it plays an important role in building understanding of the programme, sharing evidence, convening stakeholders and fostering constructive relationships with decision-makers across the UK.
You'll also coordinate advocacy activity across partners, ensuring learning, intelligence and opportunities are shared effectively and helping to build a strong network of supporters and champions for Nature Towns and Cities.
For line management purposes, this role will sit within the National Trust's Communications and Advocacy Department and report to the Head of Public Affairs. The successful candidate will work on behalf of the Nature Towns and Cities programme, with accountability to the Nature Towns and Cities Portfolio Board and the Public Affairs leads of the National Trust, Natural England and The National Lottery Heritage Fund. The role will lead and deliver an agreed advocacy strategy.
## Who we're looking for
We welcome applications from people with a wide range of backgrounds and experiences. We're particularly interested in hearing from applicants who have experience of political engagement, stakeholder management, partnership working and building support for complex programmes or initiatives.
You'll bring:
* Experience of delivering advocacy, public affairs, stakeholder engagement or external affairs activity.
* Strong understanding of political institutions, policy-making processes and stakeholder landscapes across the UK, including experience of working within devolved policy and political environments.
* Experience of building and maintaining relationships with senior stakeholders and decision-makers.
* Excellent communication skills, including developing briefings, presentations and stakeholder engagement materials.
* Experience of working across organisational boundaries and managing multiple stakeholder interests.
* Strong project management and coordination skills.
* An ability to identify opportunities, build consensus and bring partners together around shared objectives.
* A proactive, collaborative and politically aware approach.
* A commitment to inclusive and equitable ways of working.

It’s important that our people reflect and represent the diversity of the communities and audiences we serve. * Manage the trade-off between bespoke client requirements and building a reusable, multi-tenant AI Foundry capability
* Support the Management team in scoping and shaping new AI Foundry engagements, including input into proposals, pricing and statements of work

Having secured partnerships with leading cement manufacturers, we are scaling our technology; building infield pilots and showcasing the exciting potential of our ultra-energy efficient capture system to help decarbonise many hard-to-abate industries, turbocharging our pathway to Net-Zero. We are in an exciting growth phase and are looking for a senior process engineer passionate about working on innovative solutions to tackle the climate emergency. We are looking for a candidate with experience within one of the following industries: Oil & Gas, gas processing, energy generation, and Carbon Capture Storage. Join our team and help us capture the future.
Key Responsibilities
* Process plant design and support of pilot plant and large-scale plant delivery.

* Degree in Chemical Engineering or equivalent experience.

* Proven process engineering design experience with technical safety and environmental aspects.
* Proficient in the use of Engineering Software, e.g. AutoCAD P&ID and HYSYS is an added advantage.

This is an exciting opportunity for a motivated and forward-thinking registered healthcare professional to lead our Outpatients, Preoperative Assessment and Minor Procedures services, ensuring patients receive safe, effective and compassionate care throughout their healthcare journey.
Our patients, customers and partners deserve the highest standards: to expect that we do no harm (Safety) and that we make a positive difference to their health and wellbeing (Effectiveness). We want to be the best and safest health and wellbeing provider so that our patients, customers and partners have an exceptional Experience, inspiring patient and public confidence in our care.

You'll be responsible for developing high-performing teams, driving service improvement and ensuring exceptional standards of patient care, clinical governance and regulatory compliance.
You'll work closely with consultants, operational colleagues and senior leaders to enhance service delivery, improve patient flow and create a positive experience for patients, staff and stakeholders alike.

# Graduate Project Manager
**Job Title:** Graduate Project Manager
**Reporting to:** Business General Manager
**Business Unit:** GGP
---
Omexom is a brand through which VINCI Energies undertakes its Transmission & Distribution activities. Omexom specialise in the design, supply, installation, maintenance and commissioning of electrical infrastructures for a varied range of electricity utility companies and renewable energy developers throughout the UK and Ireland.
The overall purpose of the role is to assist in the design, procurement, installation, construction and
commissioning of distribution overhead line networks and substations, and after gaining experience and completing a structured training programme advancing to a Project Management role.
The post holder will work closely with project managers, designers, commercial staff and operational staff to gain an understanding of the Transmission and Substation industry and associated construction projects.
Over a two-year training programme, you will gain experience in project management, technical expertise, people management, financial management, procurement management; health, safety, environmental and quality management; business development, and commercial and contract awareness.
---
**Duties will include but are not limited to:**
* Assist with the safe, efficient delivery of work to the highest possible construction standards.
* Assist with the delivery of Projects / Programmes of work to the highest standards of safety and quality within budget and on time.
* Contribute to the commercial success of projects ensuring profitable delivery of work.
* Assist with the management and performance of operational staff to ensure optimum project delivery.
* Assist with tendering of projects and bid management procedures.
* Ensure effective communication with customers.
* Assist the Project Manager with the management of budgets and control of costs associated with the works location including timely delivery of financial and other progress data for the preparation of financial and other reports as directed by the Finance Department.
* Assist in the preparation of project progress reports for periodic review with Customers as directed by the Project Manager
* Assist with all HR related issues including disciplinary issues – at site level as required by the Project Manager.
---

**Essential**
It is essential that the successful candidate is an excellent communicator with all stakeholders (internal and external), a commercially focused self-starter with the enthusiasm, motivation and initiative to succeed in this role. The jobholder must possess:
* 3rd level education in a relevant technical / engineering related discipline
* Good understanding and practical experience of MS Excel and / or MS Project.
* Be committed to displaying the highest safety and quality related standards
* Understanding of financial management
* Ability to plan works in a logical and efficient manner.
* Ability to manage and motivate operational employees and subcontractors.
* Ability to put the customer at the centre of decision making.
* Meet targets in a commercial environment. Able to work to tight tender submission deadlines and can demonstrate previous experience of working under pressure.
* Full driving licence and access to a form of transport to meet the job requirements.
* Keen to develop/grow within the Project Management role, taking on additional responsibilities and duties.
* Ability to work as part of a team, but also be able to work alone.
---
**General**
This is a flexible based role with frequent travel to site and attendance at project progress meetings as required throughout the UK.
---
**Governance:**
Interfaces and relationships with key stakeholders:
• Project Managers
• HR Team
• Business Unit General Manager
• Clients and customers
• Team members
---

**Team Spirit & Generosity** – able to work effectively within and contribute to the Omexom team to deliver results, provide support and drive performance.

**Integrity and Responsibility** – enjoy taking responsibility for their duties and managing these effectively to ensure efficient high-quality results.

The Design Management Regional Lead will provide strategic design management for a portfolio of Power Transmission and Distribution projects covering design delivery, management and governance. Working closely with the Project Manager and site delivery teams, the postholder will be responsible for the day-to-day technical and operational coordination of OHL new build, refurbishment, and maintenance schemes, spanning access, foundations, steelwork, and stringing activities.
This is a site-based role requiring regular travel across Scotland, including to remote and upland locations. The Construction Manager will be expected to take a proactive, hands-on approach to programme and resource management, technical problem-solving, and client interface, whilst maintaining Omexom's standards for safety, quality, and commercial performance throughout the project lifecycle and offering support and guidance to the project engineers, site engineers and project support staff.

Key Responsibilities
Technical Delivery & Site Management
• Oversee and coordinate site construction activities across all OHL work packages — including access track construction, foundation installation, steelwork erection, conductor stringing, and associated civil works — ensuring works are delivered safely, on programme, and to the required quality standard.
• Act as the primary technical reference on site, providing engineering support and guidance to engineers, site supervisors, gangs, and subcontractors to resolve construction issues and maintain delivery momentum.
• Review and interpret engineering drawings, specifications, and design documentation issued by Omexom's design engineers, identifying conflicts or constructability issues and facilitating resolution with the design team in a timely manner.
• Coordinate the inspection, acceptance, and handover of completed works in accordance with Omexom and SSEN Transmission quality requirements.
• Monitor and enforce compliance with all relevant technical standards, including those specified under SSEN Transmission's project-specific technical schedules and Omexom's Engineering Management Plan.
Programme, Resource & Logistics Management
• Assist the Project Manager in developing and maintaining the project programme, including short-term look-ahead schedules, resource histograms, and activity-level sequencing plans.
• Coordinate site resources — subcontractors, labour, plant, materials, and equipment — across multiple concurrent work fronts, ensuring the right resources are mobilised to the right location at the right time.
• Manage the procurement and logistics of materials and equipment in conjunction with the supply chain team, tracking deliveries and managing site storage to minimise programme risk.
• Identify programme risks and constraints — including weather, access, outage windows, and third-party dependencies — and escalate to the Project Manager with proposed mitigation actions.
• Support outage and switching coordination with SSEN Transmission's network operations team, ensuring all planned access windows are fully utilised and safety documentation is in place.
Health, Safety, Environment & Quality
• Assist with the implementation and monitoring of site Health, Safety and Environmental (HSE) procedures, ensuring compliance with Omexom's SHEQ Management System, statutory legislation, and CDM Regulations 2015 at all times.
• Review and contribute to the preparation of Risk Assessments and Method Statements (RAMS), ensuring they accurately reflect site conditions and are communicated and understood by all operatives prior to works commencing.
• Conduct routine site safety inspections and observations, recording findings and driving prompt close-out of any identified actions.
• Support the investigation and close-out of any safety incidents, near misses, or environmental non-conformances, contributing to lessons-learnt communications.
• Ensure that all site quality records — including inspection and test plans (ITPs), material conformance certificates, and as-built documentation — are maintained accurately and submitted to the client in accordance with the agreed quality management plan.
Commercial Awareness & Reporting
• Work closely with the Project Manager and commercial team to monitor project costs against budget, flagging variances and supporting the identification of commercial opportunities and risks.
• Assist in the preparation of monthly project progress reports, including programme status, resource utilisation, cost performance, and look-ahead narratives, for submission to the Business Unit General Manager and SSEN Transmission.
• Support the identification, notification, and substantiation of compensation events and change orders under the NEC contract, ensuring appropriate records are maintained to evidence entitlement.
• Contribute to the tendering process as required, including reviewing scope documents, developing method statements, and supporting the production of programme and resource submissions for bid returns.
Client & Stakeholder Interface
• Attend and contribute to regular site progress meetings, design coordination meetings, and client review sessions with SSEN Transmission, presenting updates on progress, quality, and upcoming activities.
• Maintain a professional and collaborative working relationship with all SSEN Transmission personnel — including project managers, engineers, network operations, and environmental representatives — to ensure effective co-operation throughout the project.
• Liaise with landowners, local authorities, utility companies, and other third parties as required to facilitate site access and resolve any interface issues affecting construction progress.
• Represent Omexom professionally at all times in client-facing and external stakeholder situations, upholding the values and reputation of the business.

• Business Unit General Manager
• Project Manager
• Design Engineers
• Commercial / Quantity Surveying Team
• SHEQ Team
• Site Engineers & Project Engineers
External
• SSEN Transmission (Project & Engineering Teams)
• SSEN Transmission Network Operations
• Subcontractors & Specialist Suppliers
• Landowners & Access Stakeholders
• Local Authorities & Statutory Bodies

Essential

• Working knowledge of Health & Safety legislation applicable to OHL construction, including CDM Regulations 2015, Electricity at Work Regulations 1989, and the Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations 2002.
• Familiarity with NEC3 or NEC4 contract frameworks, including programme management, compensation event administration, and cost reporting obligations.
• Demonstrable ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, specification documents, and technical schedules.
• Strong organisational and planning skills; ability to coordinate multiple work fronts simultaneously in a dynamic, remote site environment.
• Proficient in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Project or equivalent) for reporting, programme management, and correspondence.

Desirable

## Requirements
**The role**
This is our first dedicated product design engineering hire. We hand you a loose signal, not a spec: "we think there's something here for this customer, go find it." You go and make it real, and you own it end to end, the thinking and the craft.
**Three things define this role, and you need all three.**
**First, you find the real problem.** The brief you're handed is almost always wrong, not because people are careless but because they describe the solution they can imagine, not the problem they actually have. A serving officer asks for a better map. Often the real issue is that they can't triage what matters under time pressure, and the map is a red herring. Your first job is to figure out what the thing should even be before you make it. In our world that reframe usually lives inside a constraint: the operator is wearing gloves, the decision has eight seconds, the link is degraded. Those constraints aren't obstacles to the design. They are the design problem, and often the place the real answer is hiding.
**Second, you realise it with craft.** Once you know what the thing is, you make it right, not just functional, and you build it yourself in production code. You have taste that operates below conscious thought, and you obsess over the details because they are what make the idea real, not because finish is a personality trait. In our world an interface is often the first thing a senior officer or a procurement lead ever sees of us, and it has to earn their trust in seconds.
**Third, you get there by talking to people, not around them.** There is no product manager translating for you here. You are the translation layer. You sit with an OD engineer, a serving officer, an analyst, a customer in a room, build a proof of concept, put it in front of them, and iterate on their reaction. You run that loop yourself, with internal and external stakeholders, until the thing is right.
One week it's the tactical map UI for ORION. The next it's an analyst dashboard a real analyst depends on. The next it's a customer-facing surface for AVIS or STRIDER. The brief will always be loose. Finding the real problem and realising it with craft are what make it sharp.
You'll report to the CTO and work alongside Product Leads and Business Development. You won't own the roadmap, that sits with product, but you will shape it constantly, because you're the one closest to what users actually respond to.
**What you'll own**
· The problem, not just the pixels: working out what a surface should actually be before designing it, then the visual and interaction language and finished quality of it (ORION, AVIS, analyst tooling).
· The full loop from loose brief to shipped artefact: reframing the real requirement, designing, building it in production code, and iterating on live feedback.
· Direct liaison with the people who use and buy what we build, internal engineers and external stakeholders alike. You don't wait for a brief to be written for you.
· Over time, the product design engineering function itself: hiring, standards, and the craft bar across everything we ship. This role is on a clear path to leading that function.
**What makes you right for this**
· **You reframe the problem before you solve it.** You don't take the brief at face value. You find the real problem behind what someone asked for, and you treat the hard constraints (the glove, the eight seconds, the degraded link) as the raw material of the design, not as things in your way. You know that the best product is often not a better version of what was requested but a different thing entirely.
· **You have the taste, and the hands to realise it.** You have an eye for layout, hierarchy, typography, and spacing that operates below conscious thought. Something being 4px off bothers you until it's fixed. You obsess over the details because they're what make the idea real, and you don't hand that vision to someone else to build, you build it yourself, in production code, because that's the only way it comes out right.
· **You extract the brief, you don't wait for it.** You're comfortable, energised even, sitting with someone who can't articulate what they need, and leaving with the real requirement. You'll talk to an OD engineer, a serving officer, or a customer directly, build a proof of concept, and iterate in front of them. No product manager will pre-digest the problem for you, and you wouldn't want them to.
· **You learned to code because design tools were too slow.** You're not an engineer who picked up Figma. You're a designer who learned React because you wanted to build and ship the thing, not just draw it. You write production front-end code (React/Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind) to a standard that goes live, not just clickable prototypes.
· **You build at the fidelity the moment requires.** Sometimes that's a rough flow to test an idea with a user in an afternoon. Sometimes it's production-grade because it's going live to someone forming a first impression of the company. You choose the right level of finish instinctively.
· **You think in products, not screens.** You care about the whole journey (the empty states, the error paths, the second visit), not just the happy-path hero shot. You ship, watch how it lands, and improve it.
· **You've operated with real autonomy before.** You've owned an artefact or a surface, run the loop with real users, and shipped things that mattered. You don't need a detailed brief or a committee to do your best work. You need the problem and the room to solve it.
· **AI-assisted development is second nature.** You use Claude, Cursor, v0 or similar daily and have internalised how to prompt, iterate and ship with them. It's what closes the gap between a conversation with a stakeholder and something real in front of them the same day.
**Tech you will use**
· **Core:** React/Next.js, Tailwind CSS, TypeScript
· **Design:** Figma, for when you need to think before you build, and for handoff when your work becomes a production spec
· **AI-assisted dev:** Claude Code, Cursor, v0, Bolt.new
· **You'll also encounter:** mapping libraries (MapLibre GL, Deck.gl), data visualisation (D3.js), Vercel, GitHub Actions
*You won't need day-one familiarity with all of these. At this level we expect you to pick up whatever the problem needs.*

# Assistant Company Secretary
The Assistant Company Secretary supports the Company Secretariat in delivering an effective, timely and compliant company secretarial and corporate governance service across the group's regulated entities — Polo Managing Agency Limited (PMA), Polo Commercial Insurance Services Limited (PCIS), Polo Partners, and the Lloyd's syndicates managed by PMA.
Working under the direction of the Company Secretary, the role provides hands-on support for board and committee administration, statutory and regulatory compliance, entity management and governance projects. It is a delivery-focused role: the post-holder prepares, maintains and coordinates governance documentation and processes to a high professional standard, escalating judgement calls and matters of interpretation to the Company Secretary.
## Key Responsibilities
**Board and committee support** Assist in the preparation and circulation of annual board and committee meeting calendars across PMA, PCIS, Polo Partners and the managed syndicates.
Draft agendas in liaison with committee chairs, the Company Secretary and management, and collate, format and quality-check board and committee papers ahead of distribution.
Compile and publish meeting packs through the board portal, tracking the timely submission of papers by contributors and chasing outstanding items.
Provide logistical support for meetings, including scheduling, room and video-conference arrangements, attendee management and the co-ordination of external attendees and presenters.
Support the induction of new directors and committee members, helping to prepare induction packs and maintain onboarding materials.
Minutes, actions and follow-up
Prepare accurate first-draft minutes of board and committee meetings for review by the Company Secretary, capturing decisions, delegations and the substance of discussion.
Maintain matters-arising and action logs, tracking progress and following up with action owners to support timely closure.
Help draft written resolutions and record decisions taken outside of meetings, ensuring proper documentation and retention.
Statutory compliance and entity management
Maintain statutory registers and the entity management system (Diligent Entities) for group companies, keeping records of directors, secretaries, shareholders, PSCs and registered particulars accurate and up to date.
Prepare and submit Companies House filings, including confirmation statements, appointments and resignations, changes of particulars and filing of resolutions and constitutional documents.
Assist with the maintenance and safekeeping of statutory books, minute books, common seals and constitutional documents (including Articles of Association).
Support constitutional and corporate housekeeping projects, such as updates to Articles of Association and members' resolutions, and associated filings.
Help maintain the group structure chart and directorship and committee-membership schedules.
**Corporate governance**
Assist in maintaining the governance framework documentation, including Terms of Reference, delegated authority matrices, governance maps and committee structures, in line with the approved house style.
Support the maintenance of conflicts of interest registers, gifts and hospitality registers and related-party records, and help ensure disclosures are properly recorded.
Contribute to annual governance activities such as board effectiveness reviews, governance health checks and the preparation of governance-related returns and disclosures.
Help prepare board and committee training materials and coordinate training sessions, including those aligned to the Lloyd's Principles.
Regulatory support (Lloyd's / FCA / PRA / SM&CR)
Assist with the preparation and submission of regulatory notifications and applications (for example director and Senior Manager approvals), liaising with compliance as required.
Support the co-ordination of information and evidence requested by Lloyd's, the FCA and the PRA, and help maintain the associated records.
Help monitor governance-related regulatory developments and support their implementation under the direction of the Company Secretary and compliance.
Syndicate governance support
Provide company secretarial and administrative support to the governance arrangements of the Lloyd's syndicates managed by PMA, including syndicate-level committees and boards.
Assist with the preparation of syndicate governance documentation and the co-ordination of meetings, papers and minutes for syndicate committees.
Support governance activity relating to syndicate business plans, capacity and capital, and other Lloyd's processes, as directed.
Systems, board portal and document management
Administer the board portal (Admincontrol), managing user access, meeting workspaces, document uploads and archiving, and supporting the phase-out of legacy platforms.
Maintain governance records and document libraries within SharePoint and the entity management system, applying consistent version control, naming and retention conventions.
Use governance and productivity technology (for example Diligent Entities, Asana and Microsoft Copilot) to support efficient workflow, task tracking and record-keeping.
Corporate projects and transactions
Support corporate and financing transactions by preparing conditions-precedent documentation, specimen signature and authorised-signatory certificates, written resolutions and powers of attorney, matched to internal precedent formats.
Assist with cross-entity and cross-border governance matters, including the preparation of directors' resolutions, letters of authority and proxy or notarisation documentation, as directed.
Contribute to governance improvement projects, including systems rationalisation, process documentation and the roll-out of new templates and standards.
Team and general support
Provide day-to-day support to the Company Secretariat, contributing to a responsive and well-organised service to boards, management and stakeholders.
Maintain trackers, checklists and the governance calendar to support the timely completion of statutory and regulatory deadlines.
Undertake such other duties consistent with the role and grade as may reasonably be required by the Company Secretary. **Personal Attributes**
Studying towards, or holding, the CGI (Chartered Governance Institute / ICSA) qualification, or equivalent
Company secretarial or corporate governance experience, ideally within a regulated financial services or insurance environment
Experience of the Lloyd's, FCA and/or PRA regulated environment, including the London insurance market
Working knowledge of the Companies Act 2006 and statutory filing requirements
Familiarity with SM&CR and its governance and record-keeping requirements
Experience of drafting agendas, board and committee papers, and minutes
Experience of entity management and board portal software (e.g. Diligent Entities, Admincontrol)
Strong Microsoft Office skills (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint) and comfort with new technology
Knowledge of the Lloyd's Principles and managing-agency governance
**Key Relationships**
Internal: Company Secretary and Company Secretariat team; directors and committee members of PMA, PCIS, Polo Partners and the managed syndicates; senior management; and the compliance, risk, legal, finance and underwriting functions.
External: the Society of Lloyd's, the FCA and the PRA; external legal advisers and auditors; Companies House; banks and counterparties; and other group and third-party contacts as required. **General and Regulatory** The post-holder is expected to act with integrity, due skill, care and diligence, and to comply with the FCA and PRA Conduct Rules, the Lloyd's Principles, the group's policies and applicable law and regulation at all times. This job description is not exhaustive and describes the role as it is currently constituted. It may be reviewed and amended from time to time in consultation with the post-holder to reflect the evolving needs of the business and the regulated entities it supports.
## Skills, Knowledge and Expertise
Accuracy and attention to detail
* produces precise, well-formatted documentation and maintains reliable records in a document-intensive environment.
* Written communication
* drafts clearly and professionally for boards, regulators and legal counterparties, and follows established internal precedents and house style.
Organisation

Ricardo plc is a global strategic, environmental, and engineering consulting company, listed on the London Stock Exchange. The successful candidate will lead the technical delivery of suspension system development on Vehicle Engineering projects. The projects include a wide variety of different vehicle and suspension types with a range of power sources from conventional to alternative fuels. These vehicles cover a range of different applications for various defense and commercial applications where vehicles need tailoring to meet customer requirements. The approach to delivery needs to be pragmatic and agile whilst meeting demanding customer requirements for technical specification, timing, robustness and durability. The role includes managing the development and integration of suspension systems, working alongside Design Engineers, CAE/Simulation teams, test and development teams, Programme Managers and Chief Engineers and supporting the development of junior engineers. This position requires an experienced chassis engineer with broad engineering expertise and proven project delivery skills to ensure successful execution from initial vision or concept to production.

### Technical Leadership

* Own and be technically responsible for engineering content, quality and solutions.
* Ensure design integrity, compliance with standards, and alignment with customer requirements.
### Project Execution
* Lead the technical planning and execution of suspension engineering tasks from concept through to production.
* Translate customer needs into actionable engineering deliverables through robust requirements management and solution development.
* Manage technical risks, resolve issues proactively, and ensure the timely delivery of milestones.
* Prepare and coordinate analytical design calculations, simulations, and testing; evaluate and interpret results.
* Conduct and supervise experimental investigations, including data analysis and reporting.
* Prepare project reports, including cost and timing estimates, technical specifications, and updates.
* Lead and support technical meetings both internal and external to Ricardo.
* Identify and coordinate with external suppliers.
### Cross-Functional Collaboration
* Coordinate with internal teams (design, validation, manufacturing) and external stakeholders (suppliers, clients).
* Facilitate effective communication across disciplines to ensure alignment and progress.
* Represent the chassis engineering team in customer meetings, technical reviews, and program updates.
* Lead or support the development of proposals for potential work through customer and internal meetings.
### Innovation & Problem Solving
* Apply engineering theory to address complex problems with practical, scalable solutions.
* Promote continuous improvement in design, validation, and integration processes.
* Foster and implement innovative approaches to meet evolving technical challenges.
### Mentorship & Team Leadership
* Guide junior engineers and design personnel, fostering a culture of technical excellence.
* Provide technical sign-off and mentorship on chassis design reviews, validation plans, and documentation.
* Promote knowledge sharing and professional development within the team.
### Quality & Compliance
* Ensure all designs comply with regulatory, safety, and customer required standards.
* Review product designs for adherence to legislative and engineering standards as required.
* Supervise engineering documentation, including reports, BOMs, FMEAs, DVP&Rs, and test specifications.
* Uphold high standards of quality assurance throughout the product lifecycle.
### Customer Focus

* Act as a trusted technical advisor, building long-term relationships through reliability and performance.
* Make sure all deliverables meet or surpass customer expectations in quality, timing, and budget.

* Design: has experience with or leading others using CAD tools (e.g., CATIA, Pro/E, AutoCAD), GD&T, FMEA, DVP&R, and engineering documentation.

### Communication & Collaboration
* Clear Communication: Ability to explain technical concepts to diverse audiences, including clients and executives.
* Team Leadership: Experience mentoring junior engineers and promoting a collaborative team environment.
* Customer Orientation: Strong focus on understanding and meeting client expectations.
### Industry-Specific Knowledge
* Suspension and steering design, geometry and performance fundamentals (theory), target setting
* Knowledge and experience of different suspension types (Double wishbone, MacPherson strut, multi-link)
* Vehicle dynamics fundamentals, theory and application/testing
* Heavy-Duty on and off highway vehicle experience: experience with both defense and commercial vehicles is a strong plus.
* Industry (OEM) automotive system design and development processes
* Knowledge of braking, wheels and tyres, traction control and active steering and damping systems

S-RM is seeking an experienced due diligence and investigations practitioner to join the Europe Team within the company’s Corporate Intelligence division, based in our London offices. We are open to candidates at Analyst and Senior Analyst level.
Corporate Intelligence
London
## Who we are
S-RM is a global intelligence and cyber security consultancy. Since 2005, we’ve helped companies, governments and private individuals solve some of their most complex challenges. From our offices in London, New York, Washington DC, Hong Kong, Singapore, Kuala Lumpur and Cape Town, we deliver critical insights from every country across the world. Further information about each of our five Corporate Intelligence practice areas can be found on our website.

As an experienced due diligence and investigations practitioner, you will be responsible for: * Researching, writing and reviewing high-quality intelligence reports on companies and individuals; spanning transactional due diligence, strategic intelligence and investigations, as well as drawing on open-source and human-source intelligence gathering.
* Providing subject matter expertise on regional commercial, security and political issues in Europe;
* Conducting in-depth research in English and various European languages on corporate and political issues.
* Critically analysing and assessing all information obtained during research.
* Presenting research, assessments and accurate reports to managers and clients.
We are looking for someone who is adaptable, can be part of a team, and wants to grow with the business.
The role will be based in our **London** office, however we have flexible working arrangements available.
## What we're looking for
We nurture a culture of equality, diversity and inclusion and we are dedicated to developing a workforce that displays a variety of talents, experiences and perspectives.
This is **not** an entry level position and we are looking for an experienced due diligence practitioner with a track record of researching and writing complex due diligence reports for M&A, private equity and investment clients, and/or investigations in support of disputes and legal proceedings.
We’re looking for the following experience and qualifications:
* Bachelor's degree or more, preferably in European Studies, Political Science, International Relations, Economics, Law, Journalism, a European language and/or linguistics or related field.
* Excellent spoken and written English
* Proficiency in Swedish, Norwegian, Danish, Polish, or Greek would be an advantage, though it isn't a requirement - we welcome applications from candidates who meet the remaining criteria.
* Excellent research, analytical and investigative skills, with demonstrable experience in open-source and human-source intelligence gathering and analysis.
* A demonstrable understanding of the different forms of integrity and regulatory risks that concern clients within Europe.
* A demonstrable understanding of political, economic, commercial and legal dynamics in Europe.
* Effective analytical and problem-solving skills as well as excellent oral and written communication skills.
Candidates must have permission to work in the **UK** by the start of their employment.
If you don’t think you meet all of the criteria above but still are interested in the job, please apply.
Nonetheless, this is not an entry level position, experience in the Corporate Intelligence industry is a requirement.

We offer thoughtful, balanced rewards and support to help our people do their best work and live their lives outside it, this includes but is not exhaustive of:
**From Day 1:**
* Holiday – 25 days per year increasing to 30 days (+1 day for every year you worked at S-RM, up to a maximum of 5 days) in addition to bank holidays
* Private medical insurance with Vitality (taxable benefit, tax is taken from monthly pay) - access to private healthcare, as well as to a great range of various discounts and rewards
* Virtual GP and Second Medical Opinion services – timely access to medical advice 24/7, 365 days a year, open to you and your family members that live in the same household
* Various gym discounts for you and your partner , including 50% of with Virgin Active, Pure Gym and Nuffield Health Gyms
* Dental insurance with BUPA (taxable benefit, tax is taken from monthly pay)
* Life insurance – 4x annual salary
* Pension – up to 7% contribution matched by the company. Contribution is taken from gross pay – tax relief is applied automatically
* EAP (Employee Assistance Programme) for employees and immediate family, including counselling sessions
* Free access to the world-famous mindfulness app Headspace
* Free mortgage support services
* Access to online discount hub, saving on shopping, insurance, dining and more
* Seasonal flu vaccination
* Eye tests and glasses reimbursement up to certain cost on an annual basis
* Formalised Recognition programme
* Hybrid working and flexible working hours
* Fertility treatment leave – 5 days of leave per cycle of treatment per year **After successful probation period:**
* Season ticket loan – deducted from payroll over 12 months
* Cycle to work scheme – up to £4,000 salary sacrifice deducted over 12 months **At a later stage:**
* Maternity leave – 26 weeks of full pay followed by 13 weeks of half pay (after 1 year at the company on the “qualifying week” = 15 weeks before a due date)

**The Team:** The Data Privacy, Protection and Governance team at S&P Global is dedicated to managing sensitive, personal, and non-personal information. * Act as a senior advisor to stakeholders across Legal, Compliance, Technology, and business divisions.
* Lead cross-functional governance forums to drive alignment and accountability for data governance activities.
* Be an integral part of enhancing and developing the global Data Compliance program, working alongside executive leadership to drive our team forward.

+ Lead the design, implementation, and governance of enterprise Information Governance frameworks covering data lifecycle management (creation, use, retention, and disposal).

- Information Governance Policy

- Records Retention Schedule
+ Ensure alignment with regulatory requirements, internal risk frameworks, and international standards.

- Data inventory and cataloging

+ Partner with Legal, Compliance, and Risk teams to ensure alignment on regulatory obligations across jurisdictions.

Both roles are open to the same application process; you do not need to specify which profile you are applying for.
Both profiles require a grounding in Islamic Studies and familiarity with Arabic. This is a baseline for all candidates. Profile A brings scholarly depth; Profile B brings classroom expertise. The two hires are designed to bring complementary strengths to the wider development team.

* **Primary background** Islamic studies qualification (ʿAlimiyyah, BA Islamic Studies or equivalent)

* **Primary background** Qualified Teacher Status (QTS) with 2+ years classroom teaching experience
