As a Curriculum Developer / Writer, you will create engaging, accurate and pedagogically sound Muslim educational content for a range of age groups. You will contribute to textbooks, workbooks, teacher guides, assessments, digital resources and training materials, helping Safar produce high-quality learning materials rooted in Islamic tradition and relevant to today's learners.
This role suits someone who delivers strong written work in a dynamic environment and approaches curriculum development with clarity, structure and purpose. You will apply your subject knowledge and educational insight to produce content that is both meaningful and practical for teachers and students.
You must be able to manage your workload independently, conduct focused research and writing tasks, and meet deadlines reliably. While maintaining close attention to detail, you will also appreciate how your work fits into Safar's broader vision and the needs of Muslim learners, schools and communities. The role requires developing a broad understanding of the context in which our products are used, recognising how political, economic, social, technological, legal and community factors influence and shape the curriculum we design.
## Core Responsibilities
* Researching, planning and developing curriculum content (digital and print) across Islamic Studies, Tarbiyah, Qur'an, Arabic and related strands, covering all of Safar's learning series.
* Producing high-quality student-facing and teacher-facing materials, including textbooks, workbooks, lesson plans and teacher guides, ensuring all content is accurate, grounded in Islamic sources, accessible to learners and compliant with Safar's guidelines and house style.
* Simplifying complex concepts into clear, meaningful learning experiences, applying child-centred pedagogy when designing explanations, activities and learning outcomes.
* Knowing when and how to draw on PSHE, SMSC, RE and other educational frameworks alongside Safar's own learning domains and Tarbiyah framework, applying them where they genuinely serve the content and the learner.
* Collaborating effectively internally and externally: with editors, designers, subject-matter specialists and customer insight leads throughout the development process.
* Managing your own workload across concurrent projects, meeting agreed deadlines, flagging risks early and reporting progress clearly to the Programme Manager.
* Implementing and supporting quality standards and assurance processes for both new and existing products.
* Staying informed about sector trends, innovations and developments to help ensure Safar's products remain current, competitive and relevant.
## What You Will Get From the Role
Safar's resources are used by tens of thousands of Muslim learners across the UK and beyond. The work you produce here will shape how young people understand their faith, their identity and their place in the world, and it will do so for years after you write it.
You will work at the intersection of Islamic scholarship and contemporary education, engaging with subject specialists, educators and researchers as a genuine collaborator. Producing content that is both deeply rooted and genuinely relevant requires hard thinking, something Safar takes seriously.
You will develop specialist expertise that is rare: in curriculum writing, in Islamic educational publishing and in the particular craft of making complex ideas clear for young people and wider users.

### Essential Criteria — All Candidates
* A grounding in Islamic Studies and familiarity with Arabic sufficient to engage confidently with the content being written.
* Excellent written English, with close attention to detail.
* Ability to write clearly for multiple age groups.
* Experience producing teacher-facing and student-facing content.
* Proven skill in simplifying complex concepts for young people.
* Strong organisational and communication skills.
* Experience working in a project delivery environment where priorities can shift and fast-paced delivery is required.
### Profile A — Essential Criteria
* Formal Islamic studies qualification (e.g. ʿAlimiyyah, BA in Islamic Studies or equivalent).
* Ability to reference Arabic sources and engage with classical and contemporary scholarship.
### Profile B — Essential Criteria
* Qualified Teacher Status (QTS) or equivalent teaching qualification.
* Minimum two years of classroom teaching experience in a school setting.
* Demonstrable understanding of lesson planning, learning objectives and curriculum sequencing for ages 5–16.
* Subject matter familiarity with Islamic Studies content, sufficient to write accurately and engage critically with source material, even where scholarly depth is provided by colleagues.
* Working familiarity with Arabic: able to read and engage with transliterated or Arabic-script terms and references within an Islamic Studies curriculum context.
### Desirable Criteria
* Experience in curriculum design or educational publishing.
* Understanding of industry educational frameworks (e.g. UK National Curriculum, PSHE, SMSC, RE).
* Familiarity with educational research or evidence-based pedagogy.
* Bachelor's degree in arts, humanities or education.
* Experience producing creative or multimedia resources.
### Core Strengths and Behaviours
* **A team player:** Works well with others, supports colleagues and contributes positively to shared goals. Open to feedback and committed to improving both self and team. Finds time and is enthusiastic about collaborative projects within Safar.
* **A motivated self-starter:** Takes initiative, works independently and delivers high-quality work without close supervision. Manages time well and maintains strong personal accountability.
* **Curious and a lateral thinker:** Asks thoughtful questions, thinks beyond the obvious and makes connections across ideas. Able to follow specifications carefully while also offering creative and well-reasoned improvements.
* **Resilient and adaptable:** Copes well with change, shifting priorities and fast-paced environments. Stays calm, focused and willing to learn in the face of uncertainty.
* **Aligned with Safar's ethos:** Brings a spirit of iḥsān to their work: committed to accuracy, authenticity and child-centred design, and to producing content that is both Islamically grounded and genuinely relevant to young Muslims today.

Alongside your salary:
* Learning and development tailored to your role.
* Leave: if you work full-time at Safar, you are entitled to 33 days of leave (including eight bank holidays and two days for Eid).
* The opportunity to contribute to high-quality Islamic education that will benefit learners for generations.
* A supportive, values-led working environment focused on purpose, quality and professional growth.
* The chance to develop specialist expertise in curriculum and textbook writing within a growing educational organisation.
* Access to research resources and relevant books located at Safar's London office to support high-quality curriculum and textbook writing.

### Application Stage
As part of the application process, you will be asked to submit a CV and responses to the questions below. The CV should include your job history, qualification details and experience.
**Q1: Short video (2–3 minutes)** Tell us who you are, what draws you to Safar's work and why this role is the right next step for you.
**Q2: Written response** Describe your background and the experience most relevant to this role. What have you produced that you are most proud of, and what made it good?

If you are successful at the application stage, you will be invited to an interview where we will assess your experience, behaviours and technical skills.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) can be a helpful tool when preparing your application. Should you opt to use AI for the application and written exercise, you will be required to disclose this.

Applications containing such material may be withdrawn, and internal candidates may face disciplinary action. You are responsible for ensuring that all submissions are original, authentic and genuinely yours.

Our portfolio spans fabric, wallpaper, and paint, with manufacturing capabilities through Anstey and Standfast & Barracks. Our purpose is to ‘bring the beautiful into people’s homes and lives’ and we are the proud owner of one of Europe’s largest design archives, with over 75,000 historical documents and artworks. We also have a growing international licensing programme which supports our strategic global expansion.

Licensing Strategy & Business Development
* Develop and implement the licensing strategy across the brand portfolio for product categories and partners that you are responsible for.
* Conduct market analysis to identify emerging opportunities and category expansion potential aligned with business objectives and brand positioning.
* Build a pipeline of targeted licensing opportunities across product categories, territories, and channels.
* Be adept and confident in pitching our brands to prospective licensees by creating bespoke presentations to outline the opportunities.
Partnership Management
* Manage relationships with existing licensees and strategic partners.
* Project manage a licensee from pitching, negotiating, signing the contract to onboarding, product development and marketing launch plans i.e. be the primary point of contact throughout the partnership lifecycle with internal stakeholders and external.
* Conduct regular business reviews and performance evaluations.
* Drive partner engagement, YOY royalty growth, and long-term relationship development.
* Resolve commercial, operational, and brand-related issues as they arise.
Commercial Negotiation & Contract Management
* Create tailored pitch presentations to engage new licensees.
* Lead licensing negotiations, including commercial terms, royalty structures, minimum guarantees, and contract renewals and work with legal team to draft, review, and execute agreements.
* Ensure compliance with contractual obligations and performance requirements.
* Monitor royalty reporting, revenue performance, and contractual milestones.
Product Development & Brand Approval
* Collaborate with design and brand/marketing teams to guide licensed collections from concept to launch.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

* Approve launch plans, trade events, and marketing initiatives with licensing partners.
* Facilitate communication between internal stakeholders and external partners including ad hoc department admin such as preparing/inputting into internal updates and Board reports.
Reporting & Performance Management

* Prepare regular reports for senior leadership.
* Monitor market performance and identify opportunities for optimisation.
* Manage licensing budgets and revenue targets.

* Be a self-starter with excellent commercial acumen and a growth mindset
* Be highly self-motivated, good at negotiating with strong interpersonal skills and the ability to relate to local cultural aspects

* Have strong analytical and numerical skills; you can build and explain financial models and have strong spreadsheet skills, extracting commercial insight from the sales performance data

#### **Role Summary**
This role combines bioinformatics, statistical genetics, and clinical genetics to support the delivery of genetic testing programmes from study design through to participant results. The successful candidate will process and quality control genomic data, provide strategic guidance on genetic testing approaches and study feasibility, contribute to bioinformatics pipeline development, and perform advanced statistical and population-genetics analyses where required. They will act as a genetics subject matter expert for internal teams, sponsors, and laboratory partners, ensuring that Sano’s genetic analyses, testing strategies, and participant reports are scientifically robust, clinically appropriate, and commercially aligned.
#### **Core Responsibilities**
###### **1. Genetic Data Processing, Bioinformatics & Return of Results**
* Performing participant genetic data analysis across active delivery projects in conjunction with other members of the bioinformatics team, including writing and executing Bash, R, Python, and Nextflow scripts to process genotyping array, WES, WGS, Sanger, repeat expansion, and other genetic data types.
+ This work requires a strong understanding of what expected genetic outputs should and should not look like, alongside the genetics knowledge and computational expertise necessary to identify, investigate, and debug issues within bioinformatics pipelines and analysis code where required.
* Working familiarity with standard genomics file formats and tooling (e.g. FASTQ, BAM/CRAM, VCF, PLINK, BED/GTF).
* Quality controlling all incoming genetic data against predefined metrics, running data through QC pipelines, and investigating quality failures or unexpected results.
* Contributing to research-use-only (RUO) pipeline development in conjunction with the bioinformatics team, requiring working familiarity with the languages above alongside Docker and AWS.
* Reviewing generated participant reports prior to release to verify clinical accuracy and output quality, including awareness of the clinical use and downstream reporting of genetic results.
###### **2. Genetic Strategy for Genetic Testing**
Provide input into Sano’s genetic testing strategy and support the team on feasibility and cohorting work. This includes:
* Understanding and identifying which genetic testing approaches are most appropriate for different disease areas, based on the underlying genetics, clinical context, and study objectives.
* Awareness of jurisdiction-specific regulatory requirements (e.g. GDPR implications for genetic data.
* Sourcing and evaluating new laboratory and logistics vendors, and identifying new genetic tests available across geographies to expand Sano’s service offering.

* Advising on population sizing, stratification criteria, and the genetic-strategy elements of proposals, surfacing statistical risks, assumptions, and dependencies early.
###### **3. Population & Statistical Genetics**
* Deliver advanced statistical and population-genetics analyses on large-scale participant data, if needed.
* Interpreting and communicating genetics results and concepts to internal stakeholders, sponsors, and non-specialist audiences.
* Understand Sano’s population-genetics capability, including GWAS and polygenic risk score (PRS) pipeline development, and be able to advise on their design, use, and interpretation.
* Act as the team’s expert on statistical study design and methodology for genetic analyses, including advising on power calculations, sample-size estimation, and cohort definition, and guiding correct application of statistical concepts.

* An MSc, PhD, or equivalent experience in genetics, ideally statistical genetics, population genetics, genetic epidemiology, or a related quantitative discipline.
* Proficiency in R and Python (and Bash) for genetic-data processing and analysis, with familiarity with standard genomics formats and population-genetics tooling (e.g. VCF, PLINK).
* Ability to process genotyping-array, WES, and WGS data and to query large datasets for cohorting and feasibility work.
* Solid command of applied statistics: power and sample-size calculations, multiple-testing correction (Bonferroni, FDR), regression modelling, PCA, Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium, and allele-frequency analyses.
* Sufficient awareness of clinical genetics and return of results to ensure analyses are clinically and commercially fit for purpose.
* Excellent attention to detail and the ability to produce auditable methodology documentation and sponsor-ready reports.
#### **Nice to Have**
* Experience delivering sponsor- or client-facing statistical analyses in pharma, biotech, or clinical research.
* Experience with Nextflow, Docker, AWS, and reproducible, version-controlled workflows, and a publication or conference-presentation record.
* Experience reviewing clinical trial protocols, patient- and client-facing material and providing structured clinical genetics input aligned with sponsor eligibility requirements and Sano’s testing capabilities.
* Familiarity with navigating regulatory requirements when developing genetic testing strategies, ensuring eligibility criteria and testing workflows are compliant for geography-specific sites.
* Hands-on experience performing and interpreting GWAS, developing and validating PRS, and running ancestry stratification / population-structure correction.
* Knowledge of clinical genetics.

# Data Tech Lead
**About Sedex**
Sedex is a trusted partner for over 100,000 businesses worldwide, helping them create **socially and environmentally sustainable supply chains**. Through our platform's powerful data insights and expert guidance, we simplify the management, assessment, and reporting of sustainability performance.
Our Vision is to be a leader in making global supply chains more socially and environmentally sustainable. Our Mission is To provide data-driven insights, accessible tools, and exceptional services that support businesses in improving environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance and outcomes.
**The role**
We are looking for an experienced, hands-on Tech Lead to lead engineering within the data platform and data products of our SaaS business.
You will lead a small cross-functional data pod building and evolving the pipelines, models and services that turn supply chain data into customer-facing insight. The role combines hands-on data engineering, technical leadership and architectural ownership.
You will also line-manage your pod's engineers, taking responsibility for their performance, growth and wellbeing.
We expect our Tech Leads to be exceptional engineers first — people who lead through the quality of their thinking and the systems they build.
**Key Responsibilities**
**In the First Four Weeks**
· Get to know your pod's engineers, their goals and development needs, and establish your 1:1s
· Familiarise with the data domains, pipelines and systems your team owns, and how data flows through them
· Understand the production environment and deployment approach, and begin monitoring pipeline health and data quality metrics
· Begin driving solutions within your domain, and contributing to those of others via architectural reviews
· Build relationships cross-team and cross-function, including with data suppliers, analysts and consumers
**Ongoing Responsibilities**
***Build and Lead the Technical Direction***
· You will design and build the pipelines, data models and services your pod owns, and guide their technical direction:
· Designing maintainable ingestion, ETL/ELT and data serving architectures
· Implementing high-quality, test-driven production code in Python and SQL
· Designing relational, non-relational and warehouse data models, including in Snowflake
· Ensuring pipelines and services are scalable, observable, reliable and cost-effective
· Making pragmatic trade-offs between speed and sustainability, and evolving systems as product requirements grow
· Leading through technical credibility and example
***Own Data Quality***
· You are accountable for the trustworthiness of the data your pod produces:
· Co-creating and maintaining data contracts with suppliers, producers and consumers, internal and third party
· Establishing automated data quality testing alongside code testing
· Building lineage, cataloguing and documentation to the point where others can self-serve
· Meeting governance, privacy and security obligations in how data is handled
· Making data quality and freshness visible, and holding the team to account
**Line Management**
· You will line-manage the engineers in your pod. This is core to the role, not an afterthought:
· Running regular 1:1s and providing ongoing feedback
· Supporting each engineer's professional development and career growth
· Setting clear expectations and holding people to account
· Creating a psychologically safe environment where people feel free to highlight risk, challenge ideas, and acknowledge mistakes
· Contributing to hiring decisions for your team
***Improve Engineering Productivity***
· A central part of the role is improving how the team builds software:
· Remove technical bottlenecks and friction
· Simplify architecture and data models where possible
· Improve development workflows, local data environments and CI/CD processes
· Introduce automation where it improves delivery speed or reliability
***AI-Assisted Development***
· AI tools are reshaping how software and data systems are built. We expect our Tech Leads to lead that shift, raising the capability of the whole team and not just their own:
· Use AI coding assistants daily — writing and refactoring pipeline code, drafting and optimising SQL, generating tests and data quality checks, and exploring unfamiliar datasets and schemas
· Coach your pod on effective AI-assisted workflows, including how to critically review generated code, SQL and data models, and when not to use these tools
· Evaluate emerging tooling, including data-specific tools such as assisted SQL authoring, schema generation and semantic layers, and make pragmatic adoption decisions
· Set standards for how AI-generated code and transformations are reviewed and tested, holding a higher bar where output shapes customer-facing data — a corrupted dataset costs more than code that fails loudly
· Track the productivity gains from AI-assisted development and use that data to refine practice
***Communication***
· Collaborate with Product, Data Analytics and UX early in solutioning, ensuring technical considerations are represented in decisions
· Communicate clearly, internally and externally, how the team contributes to organisational goals and priorities
· Proactively take steps to highlight risk
· Delivery
· Champion agile best practices and continuous delivery, working with Product to break deliverables into thin vertical slices that deliver value early
· Challenge the team to justify approaches based on cost-benefit and business value
· Proactively identify and work through cross-team dependencies that may delay delivery
· Foster a security-first approach
**Knowledge, Skills & Experience**
We're looking for engineers who combine technical depth, productivity, and pragmatic decision-making. You should have:
· 3–5 years' experience working in data teams at a senior level
· Strong production experience building data pipelines and services in Python and SQL
· The ability to design relational, non-relational and Snowflake warehouse data models, and a good grasp of modern patterns for ingestion, ETL/ELT, quality, governance and DataOps
· Experience co-creating data contracts with data suppliers and consumers, and integrating with their systems
· Experience driving automated testing in both code and data, using TDD and data quality testing
· Experience defining and optimising non-functional requirements such as performance, maintainability and cost
· Experience operating data systems in production cloud environments
· A year or more working with AI coding assistants, able to articulate their benefits and limitations
· Experience mentoring, coaching, or line-managing other engineers
· Excellent communication skills
· Strong experience working with Agile methodologies
· Bonus points for:
· Real-time, message-based architectures using technologies like Apache Kafka
· Expertise in ML and AI data pipelines
· A software engineering background, able to contribute to backend services and their cloud-native tooling (Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform)

By listening to their needs, understanding their challenges, and continuously adapting our solutions, we aim to empower them to achieve their sustainability goals and drive positive change in their supply chains.
· **Thinking Creatively**: Innovation is at the heart of our work. We encourage creative problem-solving and embrace new ideas that challenge the status quo. The Associate Director will contribute to developing, building and managing Shawbrook’s Financial Sponsors (‘FS’) lending activity, leading the structuring and execution of leveraged finance transactions in support of targeted levels of profitability, return on capital and origination. * Propose, negotiate and execute Leveraged Finance facilities to support the acquisition and growth of UK SME companies by Private Equity firms and investors; analyse the business and financial performance of prospective customers, ensure debt structures are appropriate to meet their needs, and identify, minimise and mitigate risks

* Actively manage ongoing relationships with a variety of clients (sponsors, investors) and intermediaries; originate business in the leveraged finance market, including participation in client and intermediary meetings, preparation of pitches, and attendance at market events and conferences

* In-depth knowledge of leveraged finance and/or growth capital structures, including negotiation of legal documentation, and a thorough comprehension of credit risk management, credit administration, loan production and servicing.
* Industry knowledge of the general finance market is desirable but not essential, including a good understanding of lending practices, structures, risk mitigation, covenant requirements, pricing and competition.
* Excellent customer service, presentation and negotiation skills, with strong influencing skills and the ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing, with all levels of management, regulators and committees.
* Good commercial and financial acumen, with capability in strategic thinking, executive-level reporting and effective business planning, and the ability to build an industry network and develop strong relationships across all business areas.
* Compliant with all regulatory requirements, remaining in good standing with regulatory agencies.
**Key attributes**
* Confident, ambitious and results-orientated, holding self-accountable, with good team-working skills and the ability to interact within a fast-paced entrepreneurial environment.
* Excellent interpersonal skills, with the ability to quickly build rapport, engage employees and gain the support of peers.

## About Artificial Societies
Artificial Societies (societies.ai) helps leading organisations understand how real-world audiences think, feel, and respond without the cost, delay, or limits of traditional research. We build large-scale simulated populations grounded in real-world data, so clients can test messages, strategies, and concepts and get insights backed by millions of responses in hours rather than months, including from audiences research normally can't reach: investors, CEOs, opinion leaders.
We're backed by **Y Combinator**, **Point72 Ventures**, and **Kindred Capital**, plus investors from **DeepMind** and **Sequoia Scout**. We're a lean team that moves fast, holds a high bar, and trusts each other to own outcomes end-to-end. Ideas win on merit, not seniority.
## The Role
Most people have never seen a simulated society at work. The fastest way to make them understand it is to put one in front of them. Some things we want to build, to give you the register:
* **A simulation of the Roman Senate**, with a live Fox News feed piped in as the day's events. What would Cato make of the news cycle?
* **Simulated prediction markets.** Take live Polymarket topics, run them through different scenarios, and watch what shapes the opinions that shape the world.
* **Whatever you come up with that's better than both.**
You'll work directly with James, our CEO. You'll live in Claude Code and Python notebooks, find datasets nobody has thought to use, wire them into our simulation engine, and ship a front end that stands on its own. Then you'll make sure people actually see it.
## What You'll Do
* **Invent and ship public demos.** Own the whole arc: the idea, the data, the simulation design, the front end, the launch.
* **Find novel datasets.** Work out what data exists in the world, how to get it, and how to turn it into simulations.
* **Make the front end good.** These demos are how people form their first impression of simulation. They need to look like something worth sharing.
* **Get attention.** Understand what travels on X, LinkedIn, Reddit, and Hacker News, and build with distribution in mind from the first line of code.
* **Feed it back into the product.** Building at the edge of what our engine can do surfaces what it should do next. You'll take that straight to our research and product engineers.
## What We're Looking For
* **You've shipped things end-to-end.** Data, backend, front end, deploy, launch. You have a list of things you've put on the internet, and at least one that people paid attention to. You can explain why it worked.
* **Fluent with AI coding tools.** You use Claude Code or equivalent daily, and you know where it stops being trustworthy.
* **Comfortable in Python notebooks.** You can pull a messy dataset apart, reason about what it actually says, and be honest when it doesn't say what you hoped.
* **Front-end capable.** You can build an interface people want to click on. Design taste matters more than framework mastery.
* **A source of ideas.** You'll be judged partly on the quality of what you bring, not just your execution of ours. We want the person whose Slack messages start with "okay this is insane but". You don't wait for a ticket. You see something worth building, and you build it.
## Nice to Have
* **Ex-founder.** A huge plus. If you've run your own thing, funded or not, alive or dead, you already know how this role works.
* An audience of your own, or a track record of things that gathered a following.
* Interest in politics, forecasting, history, or media: any domain where social opinion is the thing that matters.
* Familiarity with TypeScript (our product stack), or a background in social science, network analysis, or data journalism.
## Logistics
* **Location:** London, in-office. We build better together.
* **Salary:** £70,000 to £100,000 depending on experience, plus equity.
## Why Join Now
Simulation is a brand new technology, and most of the world can't imagine what it can do yet. This is the role that changes that. You'll have unusual latitude: direct access to the CEO, a frontier simulation engine to point at whatever you find interesting, and permission to build the ambitious thing rather than the safe one.

Send us the three most interesting things you've built and put in front of people. Then tell us, in a paragraph, the simulation you'd build in your first month and who you'd want to see it.

job_title: Senior Software Engineer, Windows/Desktop Applications - Manchester, United Kingdom
job_description:
Mission
The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.
Over 50 million people use Speechify’s text-to-speech products to turn whatever they’re reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify’s text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its 2025 Design Award winner for Inclusivity. Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies
What You’ll Do
Lead the design, architecture, and development of native Windows desktop applications using Windows App SDK, WinUI (or related UI frameworks), C#, XAML, and — when needed — C++.
Define and enforce best-practices for Windows desktop development across the codebase: code architecture, performance, memory usage, responsive UI, cross-version compatibility (Windows 10/11+), and maintainability.
Drive accessibility efforts: integrate and validate support for accessibility APIs (e.g. Microsoft UI Automation or other relevant Windows accessibility frameworks), ensure UI controls, focus management, keyboard navigation, screen-reader support, and usability for users with disabilities.
Collaborate closely with product designers, UX researchers, QA, and other stakeholders to shape feature planning, UI/UX architecture, and long-term roadmap for the Windows platform.
Take ownership of full lifecycle of features: conception → design → implementation → testing → release → maintenance. Ensure quality, reliability, and consistency across releases.
Identify, diagnose, and resolve complex bugs, performance bottlenecks, memory leaks, rendering issues, or compatibility problems — and propose robust architectural or design solutions.
An ideal candidate should have
Required:
3+ in Windows desktop application development using Windows App SDK, WinUI (or similar), C#, XAML — and ideally additional experience with native Windows code (C++, Win32/WinRT/COM).
Deep understanding of Windows application architecture, including interop between managed code (.NET) and native code.
Proven track record of designing, building, and shipping production-quality desktop applications, with an emphasis on reliability, performance, scalability, and maintainability.
Strong experience with accessibility APIs on Windows (e.g. Microsoft UI Automation or similar), and a dedication to building accessible and inclusive software.
Excellent software engineering fundamentals: OOP, design patterns, data structures, algorithms, memory management, multi-threading or asynchronous programming (where relevant).
Experience leading technical design, mentoring other engineers, conducting code reviews, and making architecture-level decisions.
Strong communication skills; ability to articulate tradeoffs, collaborate with cross-functional teams, and drive consensus.
A user-centric mindset: focus on building polished, intuitive, and accessible experiences for end users.
Preferred / Bonus:
Experience with writing automated tests for UI — unit tests, integration tests, UI automation tests; familiarity with relevant testing frameworks.
Experience with performance optimization for desktop apps (memory usage, startup time, rendering performance, high-DPI support, responsiveness under load).
Experience with localization/globalization, right-to-left UI support, internationalization, accessibility for multiple regions.
Familiarity with telemetry, analytics, crash reporting, logging, and error monitoring in desktop applications.
Previous experience in shaping CI/CD workflows, release pipelines, and deployment strategies for desktop applications.
Demonstrated ability to take ownership of feature areas or modules and drive them long-term, including maintenance, refactoring, and technical debt management.
What we offer
A high-impact role: you will define architecture, shape the future of our Windows product, and directly influence what millions of users see and experience.
A collaborative, flat-structure engineering culture — you are not just a coder, but a builder and a decision-maker.
Opportunities to lead — mentor others, steer technical direction, and grow into broader technical leadership (e.g. Tech Lead, Architect).
Flexibility, autonomy, and responsibility: you define how to solve problems, own features end-to-end, and contribute to long-term product vision.

### This is the job
Our Large Loss Team manages complex and high-value motor injury claims, including life-changing and catastrophic injuries with significant financial exposure.
As a Senior Technical Personal Injury Claims Handler, you'll manage a portfolio of serious injury claims involving complex liability, causation and quantum issues. You'll work closely with solicitors, counsel, medical experts, reinsurers and rehabilitation providers to deliver fair and commercially sound outcomes for our customers.
This role offers exposure to claims involving:
* Traumatic brain injuries
* Serious orthopaedic injuries
* Polytrauma
* Chronic pain conditions
* Psychological injuries
* Long-term rehabilitation requirements
* Significant care and accommodation claims
* Multi-track litigation
Alongside managing your own caseload, you'll provide technical guidance across the wider Personal Injury function and contribute to the continued development of our Large Loss proposition.
* Managing a portfolio of complex and high-value personal injury claims from notification through to settlement
* Investigating and assessing indemnity, liability, causation and quantum issues to achieve the best possible outcomes
* Developing and implementing effective claims strategies, balancing customer outcomes with commercial considerations
* Managing relationships with panel solicitors, counsel, medical experts and rehabilitation providers
* Negotiating settlements confidently on high-value and litigated claims
* Identifying opportunities to reduce indemnity spend and improve claims outcomes through proactive case management
* Ensuring reinsurer-reportable claims are accurately managed, monitored and communicated
* Providing technical guidance and support on complex injury claims referred from the wider PI department
* Monitoring legal, market and claims trends, sharing knowledge and best practice across the business
* Supporting departmental initiatives focused on operational efficiency, customer outcomes and cost management
* Delivering outstanding customer service and ensure claims are handled fairly and in line with regulatory requirements
To succeed in this role, you'll ideally have:
* Significant experience handling complex personal injury claims, including multi-track and litigated cases
* Experience managing claims with values exceeding £100,000, with exposure to serious injury and large loss claims
* Strong technical knowledge of liability, causation, quantum and indemnity principles
* Experience working with claimant and defendant solicitors, medical experts and counsel
* Excellent negotiation and stakeholder management skills
* Strong commercial awareness and the ability to make balanced, evidence-based decisions
* A proven track record of delivering positive claims outcomes whilst effectively controlling indemnity spend
* Excellent organisational skills and the ability to manage a demanding and varied caseload
A strong understanding of the following would be advantageous:
+ Serious injury and catastrophic injury claims
+ Credit hire
+ Fraud indicators and investigations
+ RTA and Article 75 considerations
+ Rehabilitation Code principles
+ Reinsurance reporting requirements

The Family Drug and Alcohol Court (FDAC) is a national therapeutic, problem-solving court model, which offers an alternative route to standard care proceedings. FDACs use a trauma-informed approach to help families address their difficulties with substance/alcohol use, relationships, mental health concerns and other complex issues.
Your role will require you to provide expertise, assessment, support and intervention to parents, where domestic abuse and relationship issues are prevalent and who require the specialist interventions of a Domestic Abuse worker.
You will work closely with a range of other professionals, both within the team and externally. Your role will require you to contribute to regular court reports and also to attend court on occasions to support your allocated families through the FDAC proceedings.

The ideal candidate will have knowledge, understanding and experience of working with families where domestic abuse has been a key feature, including experience of providing direct intervention with both victims and alleged perpetrators. You will have an understanding of other risk factors that are addressed within the team too, including drug and alcohol use issues, mental health difficulties and trauma. You will be interested in working to address parent’s difficulties in a holistic and therapeutic manner.
You will be an empathetic and creative worker, who is interested in working intensively with families to help create lasting change. You will have good problem-solving skills, be a team player and be non-judgmental in your approach. You must have the ability to remain calm and compassionate in challenging and difficult situations.
You will have education to degree level in a relevant field, such as social work, counselling, psychology or similar. IDVA training qualification or equivalent is desirable.

Job Title: Operations Health & Safety Lead Location: London Job Summary: Join a team defining the future of safe, sustainable, high-performance data infrastructure. As our Operations EHS Manager, you will oversee health and safety programs from early design through full facility operations. Your primary mission is simple: eliminate risk, maintain flawless compliance, and ensure our critical infrastructure runs entirely incident-free. Acting as a true strategic partner, you will bridge global corporate EHS policies with local regulations across the UK and Nordic regions.
Policy/Program Development and Risk Management: * Develop and implement local policies and procedures to ensure compliance with global Verne standards.
* Conduct hazard analyses, risk assessments, and site inspections to identify potential safety concerns.
* Develop and implement risk mitigation strategies specific to operational risks such as high-voltage equipment, battery storage systems, working at heights, and confined space work.
Regulatory Compliance: * Ensure strict adherence to all local Icelandic, EU, and international EHS regulations, where applicable.
* Oversee the acquisition and maintenance of all essential EHS permits, licenses, and compliance documentation.
* Serve as the main point of contact for external regulatory agencies (such as Vinnueftirlitið) during site inspections and official inquiries.
Incident Management & Prevention: * End-to-End Incident Management by assisting local management carry out comprehensive investigations for all workplace accidents, near-misses, and safety observations across the business, ensuring timely reporting to leadership and regulatory agencies when required.
* Conduct thorough Root Cause Analyses and partner with cross-functional departments to develop, implement, and track Corrective and Preventative Actions (CAPA) through to full closure.
Training & Safety Culture: * Develop, deliver, and periodically evaluate site H&S induction and safety training programs to meet the evolving needs of our data centres.
* Assess the effectiveness of existing safety education protocols, specifically regarding hazardous materials and safe work practices and implement strategic upgrades as required.
Contractor & Vendor Safety: * Lead the review and approval of contractor safety plans, risk assessments, method statements and permits to work via local teams.
* Ensure contractor training and competency requirements are met prior to works commencing.
Emergency Preparedness * Ensure successful coordination of fire safety, evacuation drills, and emergency response exercises
* Collaborate with facilities and physical security teams.
Monitoring, Audits & Reporting * Conduct regularly scheduled safety inspections and internal audits of facilities to proactively identify and rectify non-conformances.
* Execute workplace surveys and specialized risk assessments to ensure all sites meet or exceed local occupational health legislation.
* Coordinate and support all internal and external EHS audits, safeguarding the integrity of our ISO 45001 management systems.
Required Qualifications: * Bachelor's degree in occupational health & safety, Environmental Science, Engineering, or a related technical field (or equivalent senior-level field experience).
* Relevant regional safety certifications (e.g., NEBOSH General or Diploma, NVQ Level 6, NCRQ, or recognized European equivalents like Työsuojelupäällikkö in the Nordics or Préventeur in France) are highly desirable.
* 5+ years of progressive EHS experience, with a proven track record in a managerial or leadership capacity within data centres, critical infrastructure, high-tech manufacturing, or large-scale industrial construction.
* Sound technical expertise in high-risk operational hazards, specifically Electrical Safety (Arc Flash/HV), Confined Spaces, Lockout/Tagout (LOTO), and specialized Fire Suppression Systems.

* Design and build an on-demand ephemeral environment capability: a full, isolated stack that a developer or QA engineer can spin up on demand, run a complete test pass against, and tear down automatically afterward
* Ensure any fixture or seed data used in ephemeral test environments is synthetic or properly masked, not copied production data, given BAB rules on customer data handling and verification
* Document architecture decisions, runbooks and module usage so the environment is maintainable after the engagement ends
* Deliver hands-on training and workshops for the internal CTO, DevOps and infrastructure team, pairing with staff, including the lead DevOps engineer who built the current admin tool, on real migration work
* Define a phased migration plan that brings existing infrastructure under code without service disruption, prioritising the highest risk manual and unaudited changes first
* Produce a transition and handoff plan and knowledge transfer materials ahead of contract end, with a clear list of what the internal team owns going forward

* Experience with IaC security and compliance scanning tools (Checkov, tfsec or similar) and secrets management

Direct PCI-DSS experience is not required
* Demonstrated experience training, mentoring or upskilling engineering teams; teaching ability is a hard requirement here, not a nice to have
* Experience leading or contributing to a brownfield migration (existing manual/bespoke automation to IaC), including the judgement to assess and diplomatically integrate with tooling already built by internal staff
* Strong written documentation skills, since your output is only as valuable as what the team can run without you afterward

# Network Engineer
**About VIRTUS**
VIRTUS Data Centres is the UK’s fastest-growing data centre provider. We own, design, build, and operate some of the most energy-efficient, flexible, and secure data centres in Europe.
In 2023, we announced our expansion into continental Europe, starting with Berlin and Milan, with plans to grow further across the region.
At VIRTUS, we aim to be a positive force in the fourth industrial revolution—delivering innovative solutions while staying firmly rooted in our core values: Clarity & Quality, Accountability, Customer Commitment, Purposeful Innovation, and Capability & Growth.
**Job Summary**
VIRTUS is seeking an experienced Network Engineer with strong Cisco, switching, routing, firewall, segmentation, and data centre networking experience to support the design, deployment, operation, and continuous improvement of secure enterprise and production network infrastructure across multiple sites.
The engineer will operate in a fast paced, critical infrastructure environment and must be capable of working independently, on site, and across multiple technology domains, collaborating with internal teams and third party vendors to deliver reliable and secure network services.
**Duties and Responsibilities**
The role includes but is not limited to the following:
**Network Infrastructure Management**
• Build, configure, and maintain enterprise and data centre network infrastructure, including switches, routers, and firewalls.
• Support lifecycle management activities including upgrades, patching, and hardware replacement, ensuring alignment with supported standards and vendor best practices.
• Strong troubleshooting capability across switching, routing and connectivity issues in complex, multi-site environments.
**Network Security & Segmentation**
• Implement and maintain secure network configurations, including VLANs, segmentation between corporate and production environments, and access control policies.
• Support the application of cyber security controls across the network estate, including firewall rules, secure remote access, and monitoring integration.
**Network Operations**
• Perform day‐to‐day network activities including switch configuration, routing updates, VLAN provisioning, and network integrity checks.
• Troubleshoot complex network issues across multiple sites, coordinating with internal teams and third‐party providers where required.
Physical & Virtual Server Management
• Support the maintenance of physical and virtual server infrastructure, including routine health checks, capacity monitoring, firmware updates, operating system patching, and lifecycle management activities.
• Undertake planned maintenance activities in line with change control processes, ensuring appropriate testing, backup validation, rollback planning, and post-maintenance verification are completed.
**Backup & Restore**
• Configure, monitor, and maintain backup schedules for relevant physical and virtual server infrastructure, ensuring backup policies are aligned to agreed recovery point objectives (RPOs), recovery time objectives (RTOs), retention requirements, and operational risk priorities.
• Perform and evidence regular backup and restore testing, including validation of backup integrity, restoration procedures, recovery sequencing, and post-restore checks to confirm services can be recovered within agreed RPO and RTO targets.
**Monitoring & Performance Management**
• Support network & server monitoring platforms to ensure visibility of performance, availability, and capacity across the estate.
• Analyse network & server performance trends and implement improvements to optimise reliability and resilience.
**Change & Project Delivery**
• Work with internal stakeholders to deliver network changes required for infrastructure upgrades, new site deployments, and system integrations.
• Participate in change management processes, ensuring all changes are planned, tested, and documented appropriately.
**Collaboration with Vendors & Service Providers**
• Engage with network vendors and service providers to support delivery, troubleshooting, and escalation of issues.
• Validate external works and ensure alignment with VIRTUS standards and operational requirements.
**Documentation & Compliance**
• Produce and maintain accurate technical documentation, including network diagrams, configurations, and operational procedures.
• Ensure all activities align with VIRTUS policies, security standards, and regulatory compliance requirements for critical infrastructure
**Person Specification**
**Essential**
· A self‐motivated and resourceful individual, with the ability to build effective working relationships quickly across internal and third‐party teams.
· Excellent organisational skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders and communicate effectively across technical and non‐technical audiences.
· Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to articulate complex network and infrastructure issues in a clear, structured, and methodical way.
· Pro‐active and responsive, able to prioritise workloads and operate effectively during periods of high activity, using strong analytical and problem‐solving skills.
· Comfortable working through ambiguity, bringing structure, clarity, and control within a growing and evolving IT Operations environment.
· Experience operating within critical infrastructure or multi‐site environments, with an understanding of availability, resilience, and security requirements.
· Strong understanding of networking principles, including switching, routing, segmentation, and secure connectivity across enterprise environments.
**Desirable**
· Educated to degree level or equivalent, with membership of a recognised professional body and relevant industry certifications.
· Experience working within a data centre or other critical infrastructure environment, with an understanding of high availability and resilience requirements.
· Professional certifications such as CCNP or CCIE, with additional certifications in cloud or virtualisation technologies (specifically Azure, VMware) considered advantageous.
· Exposure to enterprise architecture concepts or frameworks (e.g. TOGAF), with an understanding of how network design supports wider IT strategy.
· Experience supporting hybrid environments, including integration with cloud platforms (e.g. Microsoft Azure) and enterprise services such as Microsoft 365, VMware, ServiceNow, and network monitoring tools.
**Additional Information**
· This is a hybrid role, with regular travel to data centres based around London, and occasional travel into central London required.
· This role comes with an on-call element, which will require the post holder to participate in an out-of-hours on-call escalation rota.

Our expertise spans across various sectors, including industry, agriculture, healthcare, security, transport, utilities, and smart cities.
### **IoT... a fancy acronym or a secret code?**
The **Internet of Things (IoT)** is like the magical glue that keeps the world connected! 🌐✨ From ordering your favourite takeaway to the ANPR technology that helps you find a parking spot, IoT is everywhere—even if you don’t realize it. At **Wireless Logic**, we provide cutting-edge connectivity solutions and technologies to ensure a vast array of devices stay seamlessly connected.
**Head of Quality Engineering** As Head of Quality Engineering at Wireless Logic, you will provide Engineering-wide leadership for how we build confidence in the systems and software that support our connectivity services. This is a strategic role focused on helping teams deliver modern, highly available connectivity systems quickly, safely and with clear evidence that quality has been considered throughout the delivery lifecycle. You will report to the VP Engineering and partner closely with Engineering Managers, Engineering Leads, Product Managers, Delivery Managers, Architects, Site Reliability Engineers and senior leaders across Software, Mobile Core, Networks and Infrastructure. The existing Test Engineers in the Software group will report to this role and remain embedded in product squads, while you build a broader Quality Engineering capability that supports all Engineering domains. This role is not about creating a separate testing function that owns quality on behalf of teams. It is about setting the strategy, standards, practices, tooling and measures that enable every Engineering team to improve release confidence, reduce escaped defects, strengthen auditability and increase the capability to deliver system changes quickly and safely. Success will be measured by visible improvements in quality outcomes and delivery flow, including reduced rework and manual regression effort, improved test coverage and release readiness, better visibility of escaped defects and quality-related incidents, and stronger evidence for audit and governance across Engineering. **This role is focused on:** * **Engineering-wide quality strategy:** Defining and implementing a clear Quality Engineering vision, roadmap and set of standards that can be applied consistently across software, mobile core, networks and infrastructure while respecting the specialist needs of each domain.
* **Fast and safe delivery:** Working with Senior Engineering Leaders,**i**mproving the ability of Engineering teams to release changes frequently and confidently by embedding quality practices into discovery, design, build, test, release and operational readiness activities.
* **Consistent standards and evidence:** Establishing shared expectations for test strategy, acceptance criteria, automation, regression, release readiness, test evidence and quality gates so that teams can demonstrate what has been tested and why it is safe to proceed.
* **Quality capability and community:** Leading and developing Test Engineers, building a clear career path and creating a professional Quality Engineering community across Wireless Logic and the European operating companies.
* **Quality metrics and continuous improvement:** Creating transparent measures for escaped defects, defect trends, change failure rate, regression cycle time, test coverage, release confidence and quality-related incidents, then using those measures to drive practical improvement.
* **Cross-domain quality leadership:** Extending quality practices beyond Software Development into Infrastructure, Mobile Core and Networks by working with domain experts to introduce appropriate test approaches, scenario testing and release controls.
**What a Head of Quality Engineering Does** * **Define and own the Quality Engineering strategy:**Create, publish and evolve the Engineering-wide Quality Engineering vision, strategy and implementation roadmap, ensuring it supports the wider Technology strategy and the need for highly available connectivity services.
* **Lead and develop Test Engineers:**Provide line management, coaching, performance support and career development for Test Engineers, ensuring they have clear expectations, strong professional standards and meaningful opportunities to grow.
* **Establish common quality standards:**Define practical standards for test strategies, acceptance criteria, test data, automation, regression, exploratory testing, non-functional testing, release readiness and evidence capture across Engineering teams.
* **Improve release confidence and change safety:**Partner with Engineering, Delivery, Architecture and SRE leaders to make releases safer through risk-based testing, automated verification, scenario testing, pre-release checks, operational readiness criteria and rollback learning.
* **Measure and improve quality outcomes:**Define meaningful baselines and reporting for defect trends, escaped defects, change failure rate, regression cycle time, test coverage, release confidence, quality-related incidents and rework, using the data to focus improvement effort.
* **Drive automation and repeatability:**Increase the use of automated testing and repeatable validation practices across appropriate layers, including unit, integration, API, contract, end-to-end, performance, resilience and deployment verification.
* **Strengthen governance and auditability:**Ensure testing criteria, approvals, evidence and release decisions are visible, traceable and consistently documented so that Engineering can meet audit, compliance and internal governance expectations.
* **Facilitate learning from defects and incidents:**Use defect analysis, post-incident reviews and operational feedback to identify systemic quality issues, improve test strategies and prevent repeat failures across teams and domains.
* **Influence through partnership:**Work through leadership, coaching and influence with Product, Delivery, Engineering, Architecture, SRE and operational stakeholders, helping teams make good quality decisions without slowing delivery unnecessarily.
**Essential Knowledge** * **Quality Engineering leadership:**Deep practical understanding of modern Quality Engineering practices, with experience shaping quality strategy, standards and operating models across multiple teams or domains.
* **Test strategy and automation:**Strong knowledge of risk-based testing, automation strategy, regression design, exploratory testing, test data, test environments and appropriate use of unit, integration, API, contract, end-to-end, performance and resilience testing.
* **Modern engineering delivery:**Experience working with contemporary software and systems delivery practices including Agile and Lean delivery, DevSecOps, CI/CD, trunk-based development, automated deployment and continuous improvement.
* **Reliability and availability principles:**Understanding of how quality practices support highly available systems, including change failure reduction, incident prevention, operational readiness, observability, SLOs and post-incident learning.
* **Metrics-driven improvement:**Ability to define, collect and interpret quality and delivery metrics such as escaped defects, defect leakage, change failure rate, lead time, regression cycle time, test coverage, deployment confidence and quality-related incidents.
* **Cross-domain technology awareness:**Sufficient understanding of software, infrastructure, networking, mobile core platforms, cloud services, automation and deployment pipelines to work credibly with domain experts and tailor quality practices to different technical contexts.
* **Governance, risk and auditability:**Knowledge of how to create clear evidence trails, acceptance standards, release controls and quality gates that support audit, compliance and sensible risk management without introducing unnecessary bureaucracy.
* **People leadership and capability building:**Experience leading, coaching and developing engineers or test professionals, including performance management, hiring input, career development and building strong professional communities.
* **Stakeholder management and influence:**Strong communication and influencing skills, with the ability to align technical and non-technical stakeholders around quality risks, trade-offs, priorities and measurable outcomes.
* **Change leadership:**Experience introducing new practices, tools or operating models in complex environments, with the judgement to balance consistency, pragmatism, adoption effort and delivery pressure.

# Senior Data Practice Lead
London
**Location:** London (UK)
**Department:** Engineering
**Hours:** Full-time
### About YLD:
YLD is a software engineering and product design consultancy, founded in 2013, headquartered in London, with delivery teams in Lisbon and Porto.
We work with engineering and product leaders who know what good looks like and are frustrated by the gap between strategy and execution. We embed senior engineers and designers inside client teams, working in their codebase, their tooling, their delivery rhythm. AI runs through how our teams work, and we help clients adopt it into their own workflows too.
We have deep experience in regulated environments including financial services, payments, healthcare, and energy. Most of our client relationships run well beyond two years. Nearly all of our work comes through repeat business and referrals. We build things clients can own after we leave.
### About the role:
We're building out data as a first-class practice at YLD, and we need someone in London who can be the credible technical voice in front of clients and prospects, not just describing what we could do, but backing it with real delivery experience.
This is a senior role, reporting to our Head of Engineering. You'll sit alongside our commercial and client services leadership in meetings where technical credibility matters, help shape and win new engagements, and stay close enough to client work to guide it and step in yourself when an engagement needs you. Alongside, we expect you to build our external reputation in data through events, writing, and the wider community.
### About you:
You've been a strong data engineer or data lead for years, and you're comfortable in front of a client as well as in a pull request. You know what good data work looks like well enough to spot it, or its absence, in the first ten minutes of a client conversation. You've probably led a team before. Consultancy background is a strong plus, but not essential if you've got real client or stakeholder exposure elsewhere.
You don't need an existing public profile in the data community, but you'll need the appetite to build one and the technical depth to make it credible when you do.
### Your day-to-day responsibilities will look like this:
**Hands-on delivery (core, from day one)**
* Doing hands-on data engineering work directly, pipelines, transformation layers, models, and the infrastructure around them, not just guiding others
* Adapting to different client contexts: legacy warehouse migrations, greenfield lakehouses, transformation layers that need rescuing
* Guiding the wider team and unblocking hard technical problems as your remit grows beyond your own delivery
* Defining and evolving our internal standards for data work: testing, documentation, project structure, code review
* Mentoring and growing data engineers across the company
**Client and commercial (core, from day one)**
* Joining client and prospect meetings as the technical authority on data, alongside our client services and commercial leads
* Shaping proposals and pitches, translating client problems into a credible data approach and a defensible scope
* Acting as the escalation point on live data engagements when technical judgement calls need weight behind them
* Travelling to client sites for workshops, discovery sessions, and in-person relationship building, and representing YLD at external data events
**Practice, talent, and external profile (growth, over the first year)**
* Owning the growth of YLD's data practice: capability, reputation, and headcount over time
* Contributing to attracting and hiring strong data engineers into YLD
* Representing YLD at data events and in the wider community as your standing in the market builds
* Supporting our sales team so that data becomes something we can proactively sell, not just respond to
### You'll have the following skills and experience:
**Leadership and commercial**
* Consulting or agency experience is a strong plus, but real client or stakeholder-facing exposure elsewhere is acceptable
* A track record of technical leadership: leading a team or function
* Comfortable presenting to senior client stakeholders and holding your own under commercial pressure
* Cross-functional fluency: you translate engineering constraints into business terms and negotiate realistic commitments
* Appetite to build a public presence in the data community over time, even if you don't have one yet
**Technical**
Not theoretical, evidenced by things you've actually shipped, and deep enough to set the bar for a team and answer a sceptical client:
* SQL as engineering: read and review SQL that performs at scale, and understand query planning, engine quirks, and how materialisation choices affect cost and performance well enough to guide a team's decisions
* Python for data: built and maintained production data systems in typed, testable Python, not just notebooks, and can set that standard for others
* Data modelling: made deliberate choices between dimensional, Data Vault, normalised and denormalised designs, and can explain the trade-offs in flexibility, query performance, and maintainability to both engineers and clients
* Transformation architecture: design transformations that are idempotent, incremental, and dependency-aware. You think in DAGs, not scripts
* Pipeline design: weigh batch, streaming, and micro-batch trade-offs against latency, complexity, cost, and reprocessability, and pick the right approach for the problem
* Data testing: know what to catch at build time (schema contracts, assertions, transformation logic) versus defer to observability, and can make that call for a team
* Data observability: treat data reliability like site reliability, with measurable indicators, alerting, incident response, and root cause analysis
* CI/CD for data: version, test, and deploy pipelines like software, with environment promotion, rollback strategies, and infrastructure as code
* Data governance: implemented lineage, cataloguing, sensitive data classification, or access control, and can hold a client to account on making data auditable and secure
* Cost-conscious: optimised warehouse spend, storage strategies, or job efficiency, and treat compute as a resource to manage, not ignore
* Platform fluency: worked across orchestration (Airflow, Dagster), warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks), ingestion (Fivetran, Airbyte, custom), and transformation (dbt, Spark)
* AI Native: experienced in agentic coding workflows (context, harness, loop, and graph engineering), and able to embed AI Engineering constructs into pipelines (RAG, semantic search, evals, guardrails, etc)
## **You should apply if:**
* Confident and credible in front of clients and prospects, without needing a script, and comfortable holding a firm technical or commercial line when a client or prospect pushes back
* Still able to hold up in a deep technical review today, architecture, data modelling, pipeline design, not just talk about decisions you made a few years ago
* Self-motivated, and want to own building a practice, not just execute a workstream someone else has defined, and comfortable without a fully defined remit from day one
* Able to work well with commercial and client services colleagues who aren't technical themselves, translating for them without talking down
* Genuinely energised by variety: different clients, different stacks, different problems, rather than depth in one domain
* Happy travelling regularly, client sites, workshops, industry events, wherever the work and the relationship-building actually happens
* Looking for a role that combines hands-on delivery with client-facing exposure and external visibility (speaking, writing, community), not just one of these

**This is a standalone role which is built around clear, quantifiable KPIs across four pillars: candidate attraction, sourcing, candidate experience and hiring outcomes. Success is measured on performance against those metrics, not on activity alone.**
**The successful person will be as comfortable building AI-enabled sourcing strategies and pipelines for a hard-to-fill role as they are presenting hiring data and trends back to senior stakeholders. # **Key Responsibilities**
## **Full-Cycle (360°) Recruitment Delivery**
* **Own the end-to-end recruitment lifecycle for allocated requisitions across multiple hubs and territories: intake briefing, sourcing strategy, screening, interview process design, offer management and close.**
* **Act as the single point of accountability for each requisition, ensuring roles progress on-plan from opening to start date.**
* **Manage a concurrent portfolio of open roles across different functions, primarily GTM, seniority levels and geographies at any given time.**
* **Partner with hiring managers to build robust, bias aware interview processes and scorecards before a role goes live.**
* **Act as a subject matter expert on modern recruitment practice, including AI enabled tools and workflows for hiring managers and the wider People team.**
## **Sourcing & Talent Pipelining**
* **Proactively source passive and active candidates via LinkedIn Recruiter, Boolean/X-ray search, AI-powered sourcing platforms, talent communities, referrals and market mapping.**
* **Build and maintain talent pools/pipelines for recurring or hard-to-fill roles across each hub.**
* **Design and execute role specific sourcing strategies, adapting channel mix by seniority, function and local market conditions.**
* **Continuously test and optimise sourcing channels based on conversion data (cost, speed, quality) rather than habit.**

* **Act as the candidate’s primary point of contact, ensuring timely, transparent and respectful communication at every stage of the process.**
* **Set and manage candidate expectations on process, timelines, preparation and next steps; chase hiring managers for fast, quality interview feedback.**
* **Run structured candidate feedback and use the results to identify and fix experience gaps.**
* **Ensure every candidate, hired or not, leaves the process with a positive impression of Yoobic as an employer.**

## Description
### About Zego
At Zego, we understand that traditional motor insurance holds good drivers back. It's too complicated, too expensive, and it doesn't reflect how well you actually drive. Since 2016, we have been on a mission to change that by offering the lowest priced insurance for good drivers.
From van drivers and gig workers to everyday car drivers, our customers are the driving force behind everything we do. We've sold tens of millions of policies and raised over $200 million in funding and picked up numerous awards, including the Insurance Claims Team Of The Year 2024 as awarded at The Insurance Post's Claims & Fraud Awards. And we're only just getting started.
That's where you come in...
We're on the lookout for a passionate, driven, and detail-oriented Claims Recovery Handler to join our growing team in Halifax. This is a great opportunity for individuals with prior insurance experience who are looking to develop a specialism in recovery. You'll play a vital role in protecting Zego's financial position by pursuing subrogation and third-party recoveries, challenging credit hire costs, ensuring every recovery opportunity is identified and maximised.
### What you will be doing
* You will manage a portfolio of motor claims recovery cases, pursuing subrogation,
* You will review claim files, liability decisions, and supporting evidence to identify valid recovery prospects and initiate action promptly.
* You will correspond and negotiate with third-party insurers, solicitors, credit hire organisations, and other parties to achieve cost-effective settlements on behalf of Zego and our customers.
* You will maintain accurate and up-to-date records across our claims management systems, ensuring all recovery activity is clearly documented at every stage.
* You will keep customers informed where relevant, ensuring they understand the recovery process and any impact on their claim.
* You will identify patterns or trends in recovery cases that may highlight wider operational or supplier issues, escalating these appropriately.
### What you will need to be successful
* You will have previous insurance experience, ideally within motor claims - prior exposure to recovery, subrogation, is an advantage but not essential.
* You bring a positive and proactive mindset, with a strong drive to pursue the best possible outcome in every case.
* You have an eye for detail and the confidence to challenge third parties robustly but professionally.
* You are a clear and effective communicator, comfortable corresponding with insurers, solicitors, and credit hire companies in writing and over the phone.
* You have the ability to multitask, prioritise a varied caseload, and manage your time effectively in a fast-paced environment.
* We are looking for a dedicated and flexible individual to join our team. This position requires availability to work 37.5 hours per week across a Monday to Friday schedule.
Joining Zego is a career-defining move. People go further here, reaching their full potential to achieve extraordinary things.
We're spread throughout the UK and Europe, and united by our drive to get things done. We're proud of our company and our culture - a friendly and inclusive space where we can lift each other up and celebrate our wins every day.
Together, we're setting the bar higher, delivering exceptional work that makes a difference. Our people are the most important part of our story, and everyone here plays a role. There's loads of room to learn and grow, and you'll get the freedom to steer your career wherever you want.
You'll work alongside a talented group who embrace each other's differences and aren't afraid of a challenge. We recognise our achievements, learn from our mistakes, and help each other to be the best we can be. Together, we're making insurance matter.
### How we work
We believe that teams work better when they have time to collaborate and space to get things done. We call it Zego Hybrid.
Your training will be delivered face to face in our Halifax office and could last up to 3 months. After that, you would be expected to be in our Halifax office at least 1 day a week. We will provide a hybrid contribution to help pay towards your travel costs and cover the costs for all company-wide events (3 per year).
### Benefits
We reward our people well. Join us and you'll get a market-competitive salary, private medical insurance, company share options, generous holiday allowance, and a whole lot of wellbeing benefits. And that's just for starters.
We are an equal opportunity employer and we value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, or disability status. If you need any support with your application please get in touch with us on people@zego.com

## What you will own
* **Salesforce.** You are the owner, not a user. Data model, objects and fields, flows and validation, reports and dashboards, permissions and provisioning
* **The numbers.** Forecasting rhythm and pipeline reporting across new business, expansion, contraction and churn
* **Lead flow and attribution.** From first touch through to closed won
* **The commercial tech stack.** Cost, renewals, seat allocation and the case for what stays and what goes
* **Data quality**. The standards, the enforcement at point of entry and the single source of truth the commercial team trusts
* **Process and documentation**. Runbooks, ownership and continuity for every commercial system, so nothing lives in one person's head
**How we work**
We expect AI and automation to be part of how you do the job, not a project you get to later.
* Reporting populates itself rather than being rebuilt by hand each cycle
* Data quality is enforced at the point of entry, not cleaned up afterwards
* Your judgement goes into the models and the exceptions, not the manual assembly
**What the first six months look like**
You inherit a documented function rather than archaeology. Every system has a runbook, a named owner and a continuity decision attached to it. You will not spend six months working out what exists.
Your first job is to take ownership of Salesforce and the reporting rhythm, then work through the tech stack with the CRO deciding what to keep, what to retire and what to rebuild.
If you have put AI into a working commercial process rather than only used it to draft, say so.
